title: Current bounding box progress and issues
body:
Okay, so I managed to go from 2 ms/collision -> 0.2 ms/collision by replacing the vanilla collision system.

1.16 system:
- I studied this for a day and am no closer to understanding it than before.
- Way too many useless streams and spliterators that kill performance
- Not portable to 1.8/1.12, easily
- Can't support 1.8/1.12 clients easily


1.12 system:
- Extremely simple and easy to understand, only took a few hours.
- Easy to change stuff around, without streams and spliterators
- Technical changes in collision order with 1.14 breaks this for 1.14+ clients


Grim system:
- Base is 1.12 collision system
- We have imported Tuinity's 1.16 offset methods as an optimization
- We are using Atlas's bounding box system, without it as a dependency
- 10x faster than the 1.16 system, without in-depth optimizations
- Collision order is correct for everyone, including 1.14+ clients.
- Really easy to add support for legacy clients and their bounding boxes.


Planned additions to the grim system:
- Caching integers -> bounding box map to avoid reading the world unsafely
- Caching bounding boxes for collision only (not block placing or breaking) - currently plants are seen as having solid hit boxes
- Whatever tacospigot or similar open source jars have optimized with either 1.8 or 1.12 collisions
- Even more optimizations.

title: Handling water bucket desync
body:
This only occurs on clients below 1.17 - Mojang managed to fix a bug!

So 1.8 (didn't test 1.7) through 1.17 all use the block place packet for placing water.  When using this with a bucket, add it into a queue.  On the next look packet, which is the look the client used to place the bucket, check to see if it matches the previous look.  This is on the anticheat thread because ray tracing on netty is relatively heavy.  If it doesn't add the hitboxes at the block, and all the blocks around it (because of god damn 0.03 + bucket desync).  Resend all of these blocks to the player, likely just using the chunk cache plus looping queue'd chunk cache updates, to avoid any issues or lag of getting blocks on the main thread, and if the player enters this area before the player receives the update, set the player back without flagging.

Thank you Mojang for fixing this, it only took you ten years.

title: Issue with stepping order after brute forcing collisions
body:
Starting position: https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/718534828017844245/875499343375904788/2021-08-12_17.01.06.png
Ending position: https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/718534828017844245/875499369959411792/2021-08-12_17.00.15.png

You are at the Y level of the block you want to step to
You are colliding on the X axis of the block you want to step to
You will end off of the block on the Z axis


Okay, so in this position, collision order is always Y first.  Therefore, you go downwards and then collide when trying to move forwards with the X movement, which goes next.  Therefore, step movement activates.

The Y movement is then set to 0.6.  It runs collisions and the player can go farther.  It therefore moves Y -> X -> Z, avoiding collision with that edge block.

The game then sets the player's bounding box downwards by 0.6 plus the 0.07 falling distance

You can step on a bounding box that logically, you should not collide with, because of collision order.


The false positive is:
[16:23:58 INFO]: [GrimAC] DefineOutside P: 1.0298738435953965 0.0 0.6181535995232357
[16:23:58 INFO]: [GrimAC] DefineOutside A: 1.0298738435953965 0.0 0.6181536120047895

[16:23:58 INFO]: [GrimAC] DefineOutside P: 1.1357948337647485 0.0 0.6434800278339026
[16:23:58 INFO]: [GrimAC] DefineOutside A: 1.1357948337647485 -0.07840000152587834 0.6434800278339026


Because we are brute forcing collisions attempting to get the right onGround status, we select X -> Y -> Z.  This means the player moves onto the block, moves down, and into the air.  This creates an offset of 0.0784 blocks because of gravity.

title: Update issue templates
body:
This PR creates 5 issue templates:

1. `bug-report.yml`
2. `false-negative-report.yml`
3. `false-positive-report.yml`
4. `feature-request.yml`
5. `question.yml`

This PR requires the following issue labels to be added to this repository (I can't PR this):

* `false positive` - issues describing a false positive
* `false negative` - issues describing a false negative
* `unconfirmed` - unconfirmed feature requests, bug reports or check issue reports
* `confirmed` - confirmed feature requests, bug reports or check issue reports

Test if you wish at <https://www.github.com/lokka30/Grim/issues/>.

This PR is not a draft - it's been fully tested and is ready to be merged.

title: 1.8 player collision buginess megathread
body:
1.8 players can phase through blocks.  Currently, this will false grim as I have no way of differentiating this from stuff like phase.  Should this be considered intentional or a bug, with grim reverting back to simply setting back players who phase into blocks on a 1.8 client?  IMO I think I should just setback 1.8 players but here's your chance to discuss this.  1.9 players can be left alone and flag phase because their clients have a different set of shitty behavior.

1.8 blocks such as chests and anvils are also broken.  A player can walk into a chest, and chest hitboxes can change at any given time.

1.8 doors are broken.  They depend on the block below or above them, without regard of the type of block.  A top door on top of stone will look different than the door on top of andesite.  I need PacketEvents to be in front of ViaVersion to fix this on 1.13+ servers with 1.8 clients.  However, I also somewhat don't care as 1.13 servers with 1.8 clients with creative mode only blocks are very rare.  And if they do exist, they can just replace the block with something more reasonable such as a trapdoor.

Many non-solid blocks acting like solid blocks on 1.16
body:
**Describe the bug**
Many non-solid blocks (e.g. doors, tall grass, flowers, vines) are handled like solid blocks by the anticheat, making the anticheat think that the player is walking through solid blocks, causing flags. It can also cause random client-side ghost blocks to be formed around the player (in the clip, red wool, but other blocks can also form such as [fire](https://i.imgur.com/TL2DKpt.png)). Right-clicking these ghost blocks updates the block to what it was before.

This only happens on a 1.16 server. 1.17+ and <=1.15 are unaffected.

**To Reproduce**
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UwvMscc2ghk

**Server Version:**
This server is running Paper version git-Paper-"fa1a7c180" (MC: 1.16.5) (Implementing API version 1.16.5-R0.1-SNAPSHOT)

**Describe the bug**
The player jumped from a high place to a wet spot on the deepslate level and signaled the anticheat with Ground Spoof.

**Server Version:**
- 1.18.2 (but using ProtocolLib & ViaVersion & ViaBackwards)
- The player joined in 1.16.4

**Grim Version (Git commit or the version in the jar's name)**
- 2.2.14

title: prediction large false when placing water near lava
body:
**Describe the bug**
When placing water near lava (creating a portal in the form speedrunners do it), grim will keep falsing prediction large. It can sometimes be fixed by removing the water, its about 50 50 though.

**To Reproduce**
[Video showing how to reproduce](https://medal.tv/games/minecraft/clips/nSZjbwzDcHPod/d1337TBFdHvS?invite=cr-MSxtcG8sMjcwNjQ0NjUs)

**Server Version:**
Current: git-Purpur-1632 (MC: 1.18.2)*
Previous: git-Purpur-1586 (MC: 1.18.2)
* You are running the latest version

**Grim Version (Git commit or the version in the jar's name)**
2.3.0

**Relevant plugins**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/59067840/172945033-f6851da5-2521-4f0d-bbdc-74b78f6b2b27.png)

title: Not compatible with Aquacore
body:
**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.

Players are not detected when the server uses aquacore

**To Reproduce**
Video is preferred.   If video is not possible, for bypasses, the hacked client name, version, module, module settings, and the check being bypassed is enough.  For false positives, steps to reproduce is fine also.

Aquacore

title: block disappeared on right-click after the speed bridge

title: [Bypass] Flagged ElytraFly bypass with Meteor (acceleration upwards with flags)
body:
**Describe the bug**
After getting enough vanilla momentum to fly upwards with elytra you can use ElytraFly module from Meteor (or any other hacked client with ElytraFly) to preserve that momentum.

**To Reproduce**
1. Download [Meteor](https://meteorclient.com/) 0.4.9 for 1.18.2 (Fabric) and join the 1.19 (Paper) server.
2. Bind ElytraFly to whatever key you like. (Using `.bind elytra-fly` and then pressing any key)
3. Accelerate enough to fly upwards without hacks.
4. Enable ElytraFly.
5. Grim continues to push you upwards, but flags Simulation.
Video is always useful. /grim log is required for reporting simulation falses.  Use /grim verbose and /grim log to get the debug information.  For non-simulation falses, a minimally reproducable description is best.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LQ65tVYfIXA
https://paste.grim.ac/NFHhD (Not sure if it's log from the video, but it should be from testing this issue)

**Server Version:**
1.19 (Paper)

**Grim Version (Git commit or the version in the jar's name)**
fdc0e88

**Relevant plugins**
(None)

Additional context: I tested it earlier with Impact (with Elytra+) and it appears that any hacked client that can flag Simulation while flying on elytra bypasses this, because it's the Grim continues pushing (teleporting) the player.

title: License/GPL considerations
body:
I have noticed this sentence in the README:
> It will eventually become paid and/or will include offer additionally subscription based paid checks.

Note that GPL requires to publish the source code under the GPL license as long as you provide binaries (selling them counts as well!).

While GPL doesn't forbid selling licenses, it does forbid selling selling binaries while not giving away the source code under GPL (and everyone the source code is given to is allowed to publish and change it under GPL).

Also note that the maintainers are not the only copyright holders (every contributor is a copyright holder) resulting in the maintainers being bound to GPL as well.

Currently, this is no problem but it should probably be considered when
> It will eventually become paid and/or will include offer additionally subscription based paid checks.

Disclaimer:
> I am not a lawyer and I have also not used/tested the Anticheat by myself. I just found it and wanted to make sure that the maintainers know about the issue.

title: ["Flagless" False] Attempting to enter a block via ender-pearl teleports you back (mostly) without any flags
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

(I really don't know how to describe the replication way, you better watch the video)
1. Throw an ender-pearl, trying to "enter" the "corner" block.

title: Setting to only send webhook in specific violation range
body:
### Feature description

It would be useful to have an option in `discord.yml` which may reduce webhook spams.  
This option will take two arguments, one for lowerLimit another one for higherLimit. 
If the option is `true`, grim will only send alerts to webhook if the violation of a specfic check is in that specific range.

If lowerLimit == higherLimit it will be considered as having the setting set `false`
Default values will be 1 and 1.

title: Build script improvements
body:
* Migrated the build scripts to Kotlin
* Removed the `plugin.yml` file and replaced it with the [plugin-yml Gradle plugin](https://github.com/Minecrell/plugin-yml) so you don't need to change the version in two places
* Updated dependencies (except `discord-webhooks`)
* Made the `build` task depend on `shadowJar` so you can run `gradlew build` instead of `gradlew shadowJar` to compile the project
* Changed the GrimAPI dependency from `com.github.MWHunter:GrimAPI` to `com.github.grimanticheat:grimapi`
* Replaced Lombok dependencies with the [Lombok Gradle plugin](https://plugins.gradle.org/plugin/io.freefair.lombok)

title: Dynamic Reach Detection
body:
### Feature description

Hi there. I have one suggestion for you to improve the anti-cheat: custom reach violations by reach
like if reach <3.1 - 1 violation 3.11-3.5 3vl, 3.6-4.0 - 10vl etc (customizable)
the fact is that some cheat clients have dynamic coverage: 3.0 if another player does not hit it, and for example 3.4 in a pvp state. thus, cheaters try to take the kick away from the anticheat. but if you issue vl depending on the cheater's coverage, this can be prevented

title: Fix food desynchronization
body:
Server version: Paper 1.12.2

This fixes the issue where the `food` field may become desynchronized if the Bukkit API `setHealth()` and `setFoodLevel()` are applied to the player at the same time.  Due to this, the player falsely gets flagged for "NoSlow (Prediction)."

Steps to reproduce:
1. player has incomplete hunger.
2. player's "health" and "food level" are restored by 20 in that exact order.
3. player right-clicks while holding food in hand.

**I haven't thoroughly tested these changes. So, it is possible that it may create other false flags.**

title: Some food for thought with 1.19.4
body:
### Feature description

The snapshot for the 1.19.4 update contains the following change in regard to networking:
> Packet bundles
>   -  Added new delimiter packet to clientbound game protocol
>   - All packets between two delimiters are guaranteed to be processed within same tick
>   - For security reasons this feature is not supported in serverbound direction

This can probably be used to nail down some tolerances of for example entity positions(especially in combination with simple Ping/KeepAlive packets), by forcing clients to acknowledge chunks of changes/updates at once. This prevents hack clients from exploiting tolerances by processing packets later on purpose, faking lag.

title: Create BadPacketsM
body:
The old `BadPacketsM` checked for `HELD_ITEM_CHANGE` being called twice in a single tick. 
This check reimplements a similar one. It checks if the client has send a `PLAYER_BLOCK_PLACEMENT` and a `PLAYER_DIGGING` in the same tick. (order is important) 
We have debugged this check for the past days (on 1.8 Client on 1.8 Servers) . It seems like sending a digging and then a placement packet while one tick is legit doable.
I have marked this check as experimental since it has not been tested on any other versions.
Flags some shitty AutoSoups/AutoBlocks. 
Edit:
Tested on 1.19 Client on 1.19 Server. Falses when standing still and pressing right click on block while pressing q to drop (Returning if player stands still for 1.8+ 21e44a2aebcc8790e82c99854326cef91c762bf7)

title: Add disadvantage for cheaters
body:
### Feature description

Hello, I come here with a proposal for Grim, to have the possibility of activating disadvantages from a certain number of alerts, for example at the end of 20 alerts of reach, to make so that the player put 50% less damage than usual, or then that he can put blows only every 600ms instead of 400ms ect...

It could be a good setback solution for PVP and especially more useful than the ban which is not very useful these days

title: HandNoClip detection
Fix 0 interval on webhook and proxy commands
body:
Currently, the PunishmentManager does a `continue;` after executing webhook and proxy commands, which means their execution counter is not increased, therefore setting the interval to 0 (which is documented as permitting a single execution) does not work.

This PR removes the `continue` calls and moves the alert and regular command code in an `else` to keep the previous behavior for other commands.

title: Always execute commands when reaching the threshold
body:
The comments in the default punishment command config say that `100:50` means the command will execute `when the user hits flag 100, and after that, every 50th flag after 100`, which is indeed how it works: it executes at 100, 150, 200...

However, I thought setting `50:100` for example would execute at 50, then every 100th (50, 150, 250...) but it does not.

This PR makes this last example work, by subtracting the threshold to the violation count before checking if the interval is met.

This could break some configs though, so I don't know if you will want to merge it. It will not break any config where the threshold is a multiple of the interval though, which I guess is what most people use as it's precisely how all examples in the default config are written.

title: Use ONLINE plugin message target instead of ALL
body:
This PR aims to fix bunch of issues with the proxy alerts by switching the plugin message target from `ALL` to `ONLINE`.

The `ALL` target have bunch of drawbacks and should be avoided whenever possible. One of the biggest issues with the `ALL` mode in this case is that players can get kicked by packet spam in certain situtations. For a plugin message to be sent to a subserver there needs to be at least one player connected to that specific subserver. In case of a empty server this can cause a buildup of messages that all get sent when a player finally connects to that subserver.

`ONLINE` target on the other hand **only sends the messages to the servers that has players** and thus prevents the message buildup. This fixes first and foremost the packet spam kicking players but also prevents old alerts showing up hours even days after they were sent when a player connects to a empty subserver that has been empty for a while.

title: Change AntiKB offset handling
body:
Cheating with basic velocity of 0 currently allows players to exploit advantages by flagging velocity without flagging simulation.
Thus setbacks will not happen until AntiKB`s violation is higher than the setbackVL defined in config.yml. 
By implementing these adjustments we can immediatly setback high offsets which are unlikely to be false positives

These changes are also particularly useful for preventing false setbacks triggered by known velocity offsets in relation to attack slowdown desyncs, such as 0.0294 or 0.042 (with speed 2).

title: Reach and Hitboxes Bypass through exploitation of the Movement Threshold
body:
### Describe the bypass and how to replicate it

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KFp5DhlXh4Y

Afaik the hitboxes of the player are expanded on all sides because of the movement threshold. 
It should also take account the players movement direction. The hitbox shouldn't expand to -X and +Z when the player is moving to +X and -Z coordinates.

Client Version: 1.16.5 but joined with 1.17.1 with Via

### Grim version

2.3.46

### Server version

1.19.4 Paper

### Plugins

FAWE, GrimAC, SkinsRestorer, ViaBackwards, ViaVersion

title: Memory leak in activePistons map
body:

Step 1. Cancel all movement C2S packets on the client
Step 2. Start activating pistons in the visible chunks

### Grim version

2.3.46

### Server version

Paper 1.12.2

### Plugins

Unnecessary

title: Fix setting slots in player inventory
body:
Grim states this can only set the player's hotbar, but it seems the info on wiki.vg was read incorrectly. This causes an inventory desync when something other than the player sets slots, easiest way to see it is putting swift sneak leggings in a dispenser and letting it apply to your armour slot. 

The wiki states:

> This packet can only be used to edit the hotbar and offhand of the player's inventory if window ID is set to 0 (slots 36 through 45) **if the player is in creative, with their inventory open, and not in their survival inventory tab**. Otherwise, when window ID is 0, it can edit any slot in the player's inventory.

By changing this, the desync will change to be creative-mode only if you don't have the survival inventory tab selected. It doesn't seem possible to detect what inventory tab a player has selected, but IMO creative mode is generally "unsupported" anyway due to its weirdness and this is more on Mojang to fix.

title: First GrimPlayer initialization too long
body:
### Feature description

`Purpur 1.16.5`
`Java 17`
`GrimAC - the last version from github`

The initial instantiation of GrimPlayer takes one and a half seconds due to the "CheckManager" and "CompensatedWorld" objects, with the first taking around 200ms and the second around 1200ms. After reconnecting to the server, everything returns to normal, with the first object initializing in 11ms and the second in 0ms.

Apparently, the initialization of static blocks is taking time.

Ultimately, this leads to an error with loading chunks on old clients when ViaVersion, ViaBackwars, and ViaRewind are installed on the server (presumably due to desynchronization, not all chunks reach the client, or it's a client-side issue). Perhaps it's not critical, but when this chunk bug occurs, false positives in Grim's mechanisms start triggering, making it think the player is cheating and notifying about Simulation checks. Moreover, it results in a quite slow login.

I conducted my checks and concluded that we can solve this issue by simply calling `Class.forName()` in the `onLoad` stage (when the plugin is loading) for each class in the `"ac.grim.grimac"` package. We can use the `ClassGraph` library for this task. The results will be similar to reconnecting to the server.

Screenshot from client 1.8.8:
`https://img001.prntscr.com/file/img001/RRe3pT-_T0W7fFIGuL7-Ig.png`

title: Check for hitting through walls
body:
This is my attempt to implement #315.

I have ran pretty much these exact changes for a while and they seem stable enough to make this PR now. I'd like others to test it.

I've also added some missing hitbox data for blocks, some have no hitbox so that they are "not implemented" as they are too complex for me to bother, but this way they won't flag the check.

When near moving pistons/shulkers, this will not be checked because those are too glitchy.

So far tested on 1.19.4-1.20.2 for months, 1.16.4 and 1.8 clients less extensively.

Test jar can be downloaded via CI artifacts here: https://github.com/SamB440/Grim/actions/runs/8815892204/artifacts/1442987269

title: Fix incorrect connecting block handling (legacy versions)

body:
This adds bundling sent packets for 1.19.4+ clients. See https://wiki.vg/Protocol#Bundle_Delimiter for more info.

The main benefit is this removes the uncertainty of the second transaction spanning across multiple ticks in the entity movement handling. If there's other areas that can benefit from the bundling, let me know.

We might want to somehow make multiple bundles if there are more than 4096 packets being sent? I'll look into this if this is a concern

title: Kick players for sending invalid transactions
body:
1.7 - 1.16.5 clients use the `WINDOW_CONFIRMATION` packet:
```java
// MCP 1.8 - NetHandlerPlayClient.java#L1049
addToSendQueue(new PacketConfirmTransaction(packetIn.getWindowId(), packetIn.getActionNumber(), true));
```
`accepted` is always `true` in the client's response.

Some hacked client modules (Blink/FakeLag/Disabler) or some type of bots may not send this packet correctly and just return all the values sent by the server.
Since the server is sending `accepted=false`, the client will also reply `accepted=false` in this case.
This is impossible. I implemented a check that simply disconnects players that reply incorrectly.

Tested on a stable production environment.

title: Implement BadPacketsT to check for invalid hitboxes
body:
Right clicking a player results in a `WrapperPlayClientInteractEntity` with the action `INTERACT_AT`.
The `INTERACT_AT` action has a `Vector3f` called `targetVector` or `target`. The client sends the hitbox at which it interacts with the entity to the server. Most hitbox cheats do not change (spoof) these values which means we can easily detect any hitbox modification when the player interacts with an entity even when the player is not hitting outside of the hitbox. I implemented a check that checks the hitbox size for players.

Note: This check should never false flag.

Tested on a stable production environment.

title: Invincibility issue
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

Related to #1139 which was closed due to lack of information.

Sometimes one player is invincible to hand-on-hand pvp (excluding arrows) and the other player automatically wins because of it. The problem can be resolved by teleporting the player to spawn, as the affected player becomes untracked by others.

Upon analyzing the `PlayInUseEntity` packet, we found out that Grim cancels the packet, leading to damage cancellation. The suspected cause is the Reach check in Grim at:
https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/blob/0a36d3e92ebfe9a6cc6f28e003b8d9787df16f9c/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/checks/impl/combat/Reach.java#L75

This indicates that the packet is being canceled because Grim removes the entity from the `player.compensatedEntities.entityMap` but not from the `player.compensatedEntities.serverPositionsMap`. If the player has the entity removed from the `serverPositionsMap` then the problem doesn't happen at all.

Some observations:

- This issue only happens in fast-paced game modes with quick teleports between worlds and distant chunks, leading to rapid player tracking changes.
- The `serverPositionsMap` is not removed in the real tick, unlike the `entityMap`, potentially contributing to the bug's occurrence. Although I'm not so sure about the exact role of the `serverPositionsMap`.
- When changing worlds, the `serverPositionsMap` is not cleared according to Grim's source, though it's also unclear if this is the root cause.

To address this, we implemented a temporary solution, we manually remove the entity from `serverPositionsMap` if it exists in `serverPositionsMap` but not in `entityMap`. However, we acknowledge that this might not be the most elegant fix, so we wonder if there's a better solution on Grim's end.

### Grim version

[0a36d3e](https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/commit/0a36d3e92ebfe9a6cc6f28e003b8d9787df16f9c)

title: Forge Mods Placeholder & Join Commands
body:
### Feature description
Forge clients send a list of installed mods when joining a server, however I believe they stopped doing this in modern versions (about 1.17). Configurable join commands could be implemented, which would (as the name implies) executes a command on join (commands should happen in the order they are specified in the config), an example config can be found below (the same could be done for brands). A placeholder could be added for the the player's forge mods, `%mods%` or `%forge_mods%` for example. The format could be as seen below, or `No Forge Mods` if the packet isn't sent.
```yaml
Forge mods (2):
  skinlayers3d 1.2.0
  foamfix 0.6.3a
```
```yaml
# a better name should be used
forge_mod_join_commands:
  # if a player joins with foamfix and 3dskinlayers,
  # they will get kicked for "FoamFix 0.6.3a is not allowed!"
  # then banned for "3dSkinLayers is not allowed!"
  foamfix:
    version: 0.6.3a
    command: kick %player% FoamFix 0.6.3a is not allowed!
  skinlayers3d:
    version: *
    command: ban %player% 3dSkinLayers is not allowed!
```

body:
### Feature description

packetevents uses ConcurrentHashMap to save listeners, this means that listeners of the same priority will be executed out of order
This can make some surprises, for example switchitem noslow can make ghostblocks(Rise abused it for a while), probably because CheckManagerListener executes before PacketPlayerDigging
~~or change the priority of other listeners to normal or higher to prevent this?~~

title: Shaded Kotlin causes other plugins to fail with `ClassCastException`s
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

title: Basic interact check
body:
### Feature description

### The Suggestion
Hello, I would like to suggest adding an interaction check to Grim because currently, there is none. At the moment, the most needed check is to detect if a player is interacting with chests behind a wall or attacking another player behind a block (this is especially common for cheaters who use cheats to attack through cobwebs on certain PvP servers).

### Why It Fits Grim Anticheat?
I believe that it would be possible to create a check that is mathematically impossible to bypass since it would only need to trace where the player was looking, and if there are any blocks between the player who is interacting and the object that the player is trying to interact with. I think that a check like this would fit Grim's "philosophy" perfectly.

I know that this shouldn't be really hard for all the talented creators and contributors of Grim anticheat ;) Thanks.

title: False Positive Detection with Aquatic Helmet in Grim Anticheat
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

I encountered a false positive detection issue with the Grim Anticheat, version 2.3.62, on my Purpur server (version 1.20.4). The problem arises when a player equips a helmet enchanted with Aqua Affinity III. Specifically, when the player who is wearing this helmet starts moving underwater, the anti-cheat system erroneously flags and blocks them for a "simulation violation". This issue can be consistently replicated by following these steps:
Ensure Grim Anticheat 2.3.62 is installed and active on a server running Purpur 1.20.4.
Equip a helmet with the Aqua Affinity III enchantment.
Enter any body of water and start moving underwater.
Observe the anti-cheat alerts for a simulation violation concerning the player's movement.

### Grim version

2.3.62

### Server version

Purpur 1.20.4

title: Don't shade packetevents anymore
body:
### Feature description

Pros of unshaded packetevents:

- Increased performance, multiple plugins using packet events can share the same instance.
- Allows server owners to update packet events without waiting on grim to do it.
- Halves grims jar size
- Seperation of concerns
- @retrooper gets credit for his work (Downloads for shaded packet events aren't counted, if unshaded he gets downloads/recognition/ad revenue)

Cons:
- Server owners need to download 2 jars, one for packet events one for grim

title: Create plugin.yml automatically
body:
Define deprecated `plugin-yml.bukkit` before because it didn't support Folia. Since then, `plugin-yml.bukkit` updated and it supports Folia since [release 0.6.0](<https://github.com/Minecrell/plugin-yml/releases/tag/0.6.0>). This PR adds `plugin-yml.bukkit` back.

#### Benefits:
Automatically generating the `plugin.yml` means that you don't need to change the version, description, etc. twice anymore (`build.gradle.kts` & `plugin.yml`)

title: Compile with Java 17 - drop Java 8, Java 11
body:
### Feature description

As of the latest versions of ViaVersion, Java 17 has been required to run Via.
I've tested things out to verify their claim in regards of 1.8 running on java 17 and I can confirm this works (what I used was: paper 1.8, pandaspigot 1.8 - recommended to use over paper).
I believe there's no need for us to support Java 8, Java 11 and only Java 17 and higher as of the next versions of Grim.
ViaVersion latest release: https://github.com/ViaVersion/ViaVersion/releases/tag/5.0.0

title: MultiAura/KillAura without move fix
body:
### Describe the bypass and how to replicate it

For the KillAura use LiquidBounce. In general they work like this:

For each entity, send a stupidity packet looking at the entity and attack the entity. Once done send another stupidity packet with the real player's yaw and pitch.

I think it can be fixed by ignoring duplicate packets in the reach check, it worked for me without falses.

Latest commit

The grim spectate command uses player.teleport which is not supported on folia. For folia the function player.teleportAsync would be needed but that would break java 8 compatability. I'm currently looking into that to see if there is a way to maybe load some classes if the plugin runs on folia to fix that. I'm open for ideas :D

any

Any folia version

title: Attribute rework
body:
This rewrites the attribute system and also moves Grim towards using the attribute system more widely instead of manually checking client versions everywhere. 

Attributes have a version requirement, if the player is below a version where that attribute exists then changes sent by the server will be ignored. They also have a get rewriter, this allows modification of the attribute value before being returned, which allows for contextual stuff like checking the player's version.

Fixes #1583

Tested on 1.20.6 and 1.21 server and clients with via.

Latest build: https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/actions/runs/10333304179/artifacts/1798102852

title: Check the bow noslow
body: I read the previous topic, and I know that grimac can't detect bow noslow through simulation check. Then why not do a non-simulation test to detect bow noslow? Just like the matrix anti-cheating plug-in and nocheatplus anti-cheating plug-in, these anti-cheating plug-ins take advantage of speed limit to check the bow noslow. So I think grimac should check the bow noslow to prevent some bypasses.

title: Add a good autoclick detection
body:
### Feature description

On PVE server (or skyblock server, servers with spawners) player can easily abuse with autoclick to click at the perfect interval (580ms) and get unfair advantage.

We tried to do a custom plugin to check each time between player click that is validated by the server, but it can't be really used as it's per tick, and even with autoclick we get up to 150ms difference, and a legit player can achieve the same difference of 150ms
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b7222b0-20fd-4c1b-b1bf-e11b5c1b95fe)

We saw that to make it better we would need to the player movement, but way more hard to do, as you need to play with packets, and require more knowledge.

If someone could add a perfect way to be 95% sure a player is autoclicking, I am willing to pay

### How To Fix

```java
//CompensatedWorld.java, line 506

} else if (state.getType() == StateTypes.REPEATER) {
            return state.getFacing() == face && state.isPowered() ? state.getPower() : 0;
        }
        
Should be changed to:

} else if (state.getType() == StateTypes.REPEATER) {
            return state.getFacing() == face && state.isPowered() ? 15 : 0;
        }

Because repeaters don't have a power level, they are always 15(?) power

title: Adding support for custom climbables.
body:
### Feature description

The amount of blocks that are climbable can be extended via a datapack in climbables.json. However this results in false simulation checks with Grim.

I have set chains to be climbable via a datapack, climbing the chain results in falses from Grim. The default vanilla climbables work fine.

I would like to see support for using more blocks as climbables. If this is not possible due to not being able to read what blocks are climbable, perhaps let the user define climbable blocks in the config?

title: Add a check to prevent placing block while looking at a wrong block face
body:
This check is designed to prevent players from exploiting the scaffold mechanic in a way that allows them to place blocks beneath themselves without properly aiming at the correct face of the previous block. Specifically, it ensures that players cannot place a block directly beneath them unless they are actually looking at the correct face of the block they intend to place it against.

title: Check Line of Sight of Player Before Block Placements and Opening Containers

labels.name: status: rebase required
labels.description: The pull request needs rebasing onto the merge branch

body:
This prevents players from using Freecam and interacting with blocks through walls. For example, accessing a chest behind a wall they shouldn't have access to.

Can be used to check all block interactions, but currently only checks containers for maximum performance. The list of blocks being interacted with to check will be configurable to all or a list.

This also prevents laggy players from being able to break a block in regions protected by plugins such as Worldguard and quickly opening a container behind it before the block reappears client side.

Currently making a PR To ask for feedback on:
- What changes, if any, need to be made for **latency compensation**.
- If suggested **configuration options** are appropriate
- What the result of using the **Player.BLOCK_INETRACTION_RANGE** attribute will have for players on < 1.20.5
- Note that the existing code has comments and print statements to make it more clear what's going on that may not be in the final PR.

EDIT: This could have the potential to close https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/issues/1498

title: Optimizing getPossibleEyeHeights()
body:
This PR makes getPossibleEyeHeights() return double[] and in Standing -> Sneaking -> Elytra order, which is far more likely, reducing the number of average iterations taken in practice to process these checks. In addition, there's no reason to use the list object over the more efficient primitive type, which this PR also changes.

getPossibleEyeHeights() is called for 5 checks in the current codebase. In most cases, its return values are iterated over in a loop to verify some player behavior's like reach or block placement is legitimate. In each of these cases it is far more likely that the player is standing than say flying on an elytra or swimming and hitting an entity.

body:
This PR introduces the possibility to display a player's violations by adding the /grim history <player> command. When triggered, the command will show something like this:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3f0159a-75ba-46c7-8084-7aada61706ec)

The PR also adds the "[log]" command for punishments.yml, which inserts the violation to the player's history

This change is extremely useful, as it makes it much easier to determine whether or not player is cheating.

title: Ensure ComplexCollisionBoxes can only contain SimpleCollisionBoxes
body:
Three core changes that are tied together
- Ensure ComplexCollisionBoxes can only contain SimpleCollisionBoxes
   - Flattening out ComplexCollisionBoxes reduces complexity and increases performance. Also may allow us to primitize more of this class in the future.
- Add a new .downCast() method to all CollisionBoxes that uses primitive arrays and port the codebase to use this new method.
    - This method does not "clear out" the array passed to it but it returns a "size" representing the elements contained in the passed in array that should be iterated over. Using elements in the array past the returned size may lead to undefined behaviour.  
    - The legacy method is still used in Collisions.java in the Tuinity-based collision handling code. This can be ported eventually if performance is still lackluster after merging this PR.
    - SIMD and Unsafe are viable tactics we can use to get even more performance for future reference. 
- Optimize ComplexCollisionBoxes to use primitives to store data internally. Speeds up all methods in this class.
    - We can reduce memory usage by manually managing the maximum size of these ComplexCollisionBoxes. The default is 15 for the size of the modern Cauldron (most complex shape) but this can be managed for individual blocks for memory optimization.

title: Fix race condition and exception when registering check permissions during rapid consecutive player joins on server start
body:
When consecutive players join the server rapidly and they are the first joining players, a data race occurs and the permissions for the checks are registered multiple times causing an exception:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/abdfa137-0d83-4539-9217-673a51986c61)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0de89644-45e3-48c5-bb0a-b121fe579d16)

Explanation of the data race:

1. The `init()` method is invoked on Netty threads whenever a player joins the server.
2. The `inited` variable is a non-thread-safe `static boolean` used to determine if initialization has already occurred.
3. The `inited` flag is checked early to return if initialization is complete. However, this check is not thread-safe.
4. Due to the data race on `inited`, if multiple players join rapidly, multiple threads can proceed past the `if (inited)` check, causing `addPermission` to be called multiple times concurrently.

title: Fix AirLiquidPlace falses (and BadPacketsX false)

labels.name: status: review required
labels.description: The pull request is awaiting review

body:
The comments in the code explain everything very clearly and in detail.

This also indirectly fixes a BadPacketsX false which is triggered together when AirLiquidPlace fails in rapid succession multiple times in a tick.


```
    /* This check has been plagued by falses for ages, and I've finally figured it out.
    When breaking and placing on the same tick in the same tick, I believe the vanilla client always sends DIGGING ACTION packets first
    This check's falses all seem to stem from processing DiggingAction.START_DIGGING before PacketType.Play.Client.PLAYER_BLOCK_PLACEMENT in the same tick
    Since we process the break first, when we go to process the place it looks like the player placed against air in the async world
    We will often see:
        Async world updated: short_grass -> air at X: -32, Y: 69, Z: -240, tick 0, cause/source: DiggingAction.START_DIGGING
        AirLiquidPlace Check: Block state at X: -32, Y: 69, Z: -240 is air (valid: false), tick +0-1, cause/source: PacketType.Play.Client.PLAYER_BLOCK_PLACEMENT <---- previously falsed here
        Async world updated: air -> short_grass at X: -32, Y: 69, Z: -240, tick +3-4, cause: realtime task in applyBlockChanges(List<Vector3i> toApplyBlocks) source: PacketType.Play.Client.PONG
        Async world updated: short_grass -> air at X: -32, Y: 69, Z: -240, tick +0-1, cause: handleNettySyncTransaction(LatencyUtils.java:56) source: PacketType.Play.Client.PONG
    In addition, it is possible for:
        Async world updated: short_grass -> air at X: -49, Y: 69, Z: -190, tick 0, cause: realtime task in applyBlockChanges(List<Vector3i> toApplyBlocks) source: PacketType.Play.Client.PONG
        AirLiquidPlace Check: Block state at X: -49, Y: 69, Z: -190 is air (valid=false), tick 0 <--- false due to change from applyBlockChanges()
        Async world updated: grass_block[snowy=false] -> grass_block[snowy=false] at X: -49, Y: 69, Z: -189, tick 0, cause: handleNettySyncTransaction(LatencyUtils.java:56) source: PacketType.Play.Client.PONG
    And in even more rare cases:
        Async world updated: air -> air at X: -51, Y: 71, Z: -179, tick 0, cause: handleNettySyncTransaction(LatencyUtils.java:56) source: PacketType.Play.Client.PONG
        AirLiquidPlace Check: Block state at X: -49, Y: 70, Z: -180 is short_grass (valid=true), tick 0
        Async world updated: short_grass -> air at X: -49, Y: 70, Z: -180, tick 1, cause/source: DiggingAction.START_DIGGING <--- double dig here (see my BadPacketsX patch) this is legit behaviour. Can only be up to 2 in 1 tick though.
        Async world updated: air -> short_grass at X: -49, Y: 70, Z: -180, tick 1, cause/source: DiggingAction.START_DIGGING
        Async world updated: short_grass -> air at X: -51, Y: 70, Z: -179, tick 1, cause: realtime task in applyBlockChanges(List<Vector3i> toApplyBlocks) source: PacketType.Play.Client.PONG
        AirLiquidPlace Check: Block state at X: -49, Y: 70, Z: -179 is air (valid=false), tick 2 <--- falses here due to double dig if we only check the latest changed blockstate. We have to check all changes at the location in same tick.
        AirLiquidPlace Check: Block state at X: -49, Y: 70, Z: -179 is air (valid=true), tick 2
        All of which previously would've caused a false.
        To solve this we store recently changed blocks caused by DiggingAction.START_DIGGING (instant breaking) and check against the old block.
        Lots of other checks have similar issues, and with the new player.blockHistory we can patch those.
    So that's it right? It's unfalsable?
        Very close but not quite. Vanilla's client game desyncs, especially on a laggy connection where a player is breaking and placing grass 20 cps/sec in the same tick
        it is possible for short grass to be interacted with even if server-side the block is air much later, and it won't be accounted for because the modification isn't recent.
        This is incredibly rare, unreliable and is only triggerable if you intentionally want to false the check. Enough so that I consider a violation lvl of 2-3 to be perfect.
    */
```

EDIT: fixes https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/issues/1508, https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/issues/1403 and https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/issues/1776

title: Speeding up Grim - Adding SIMD support
body:
As our codebase grows with more checks, performance has and will become increasingly important. 

This code here provides the basic structure necessary to add support for running operations with SIMD, and falling back on scalar operations when they are available at **no runtime performance cost** even in cases where SIMD is not available. Java 18 is the minimum requirement.

There are many parts of the code that can/may have to be change in order to take full advantage of SIMD. This PR Draft does not do that.

If there's interest, I'll consider also updating this draft to include Project Panama native code setup as well. We can include or download a small native library at runtime and our fall back order would look something like Native Code (probably SIMD) -> Java SIMD -> Scalar

Players Falling Through the Ground on Login, World Change, or Teleport
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

**Title:** Players Falling Through the Ground on Login, World Change, or Teleport

**Description:**
We have been using Grim for the past few days. After initial issues with a large number of false logs, we managed to get it running somehow.

We have granted all players the permission `grim.nosetback`, which should prevent them from being set back. Despite this, the following bug is occurring:

**Bug:** Players fall through the ground when:

- This bug does not always occur but happens frequently enough to be a concern.
- Logging in,
- Changing worlds, or
- Rarely during teleportation.

This happens specifically when the ground is only one block thick.

**Expected Behavior:**
Players should not fall through the ground under any circumstances, especially when the `grim.nosetback` permission is applied.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Grant the `grim.nosetback` permission to a player.
2. Set up a scenario where the ground is only one block thick.
3. Have the player:
   - Log in,
   - Change worlds, or
   - Teleport.
4. Observe if the player falls through the ground.

**Environment:**

- Grim Version: [current Version from main branch]
- Server Version: [Paper 1.21.3]

**Additional Notes:**
We would appreciate a quick fix for this issue. If there are any checks that we can temporarily disable to work around this problem, we would also be grateful for that information.

current build from main branch

Paper ~ 1.21.3

GrimAC

title: RotationPlace false positive
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

happens on older versions only i think, on line 102 a comment falsely assumes that the latest rotation is always up to data when placing. However this is not true at all. Since on 1.8.9 the placing of blocks gets handled before sending the player position packet. So if the yaw or pitch changed on the tick that you place a block grim will flag you. 
I suggest somehow waiting with verifying the rotation until the PlayerPositionPacket is send so that you can use the latest rotation and properly check the placement.

to test this just boot up 1.8.9 and start placing blocks while moving your mouse quickly

title: Fix legacy (< 1.16.2) hitbox modeling for close non-relative teleports

labels.name: status: review required
labels.description: The pull request is awaiting review

body:
I've been furiously trying to figure out what the causes of missed hitbox falses are. They seem to happen at random inconsistently, and rarely.

At least in regards to legacy versions, I may have found the answer (or at least one contributing factor). 

When receiving a teleport packet from the server (which happens periodically to synchronize entity positions even if the entity isn't being teleported) if the teleport packet moves the entity by less than 0.03125D in the X and Z directions and less than 0.015625D in the Y axis then the entity won't actually be moved client side.

However @SamB440 while trying to implement handling for this I noticed that you had a section with some code below it commenting about how we need to do some / 32 unpacking because of Via, yet in the actual code you don't check for via usage and just apply the position change if the player version is < 1.9 regardless if via is being used or not. Could you please clarify the code with additional comments and/or explain what's going on and if this is correct?

This should *hopefully* fix or at least contribute to fixing @ItsClairton described reach falses with Elder Guardians

title: Fix nosuchmethoderror in grimversion in old minecraft versions
body:
This PR fixes a NoSuchMethodError when running /grim version. The issue was caused by using a Gson method introduced in version 2.8.6, while older versions like Minecraft 1.8.8 include an earlier Gson version. This update ensures compatibility with the older Gson version.

The method used in this PR is deprecated, but I think it's unlikely to be removed anytime soon.

title: BadPacketsV: fix >= 1.21.2 false flag

labels.name: status: review required
labels.description: The pull request is awaiting review

body:
The experimental BadPacketsV check falses for vanilla >= 1.21.2 clients when standing still.

Vanilla clients send these movement packets when the player doesn't move:

- version 1.8: Every 21st packet includes a position (20 onground only packets inbetween).
- at least since version 1.12 (possibly changed somewhere between 1.9 and 1.11): Every 20th tick sends a position (19 ticks without a movement packet inbetween).

This is caused by a change in the onUpdateWalkingPlayer (MCP) / sendMovementPackets (Yarn) method: In older versions, the movement packet is sent and the "ticks since position" counter is incremented. If a position was sent, it is set back to 0. In newer versions, the increment happens before the conditions are evaluated, so the counter isn't really reset to 0 when sending a position, but rather to 1. This means there is one fewer tick between two position packets.

To fix this, I changed the noReminderTicks comparison to < 19.

Edit: The falses only affected >= 1.21.2 players and not >= ~1.12 players. Also, >= 1.21.2 players on < 1.21.2 servers did not false this because we do not support the end tick packet there due to ViaVersion.

{languageVersion=17, vendor=any vendor, implementation=vendor-specific}.```

Caused by: org.gradle.jvm.toolchain.internal.ToolchainDownloadFailedException:

title: Fix a rare CME in LatencyUtils

labels.name: status: review required
labels.description: The pull request is awaiting review

body:
## Problem
The original implementation of `handleNettySyncTransaction` could throw a ConcurrentModificationException if a runnable task modified the `transactionMap` (either directly or by calling `addRealTimeTask`). This was observed on Folia servers but could theoretically occur in any environment.

## Solution
Refactored `handleNettySyncTransaction` to use a two-pass approach:
1. First pass: Collect tasks and remove them from `transactionMap` using the iterator
2. Second pass: Execute the collected tasks

Added a class-level `ArrayList<Runnable>` to store tasks between passes, which is cleared and reused each call to avoid unnecessary allocations.

## Implementation Details
- Added `private final ArrayList<Runnable> tasksToRun` field
- Split the original single loop into collection and execution phases
- Maintained synchronization around both phases to preserve thread safety
- Added detailed comments explaining the approach and rationale
- Chose not to use a ConcurrnetLinkedQueue because iteration may not reflect state of data structure and working to ensure this is always correct for our use case was too complicated

## Performance Considerations
- Using ArrayList for `tasksToRun` as it only needs sequential adds and iteration
- Keeping it as a class field to reuse the backing array
- Maintained LinkedList for `transactionMap` due to its frequent size changes and removal patterns

## Testing
- Verified on local server
- Seems to be working, used in prod by lifestealsmp.com who originally reported the issues and hasn't happened again.

This change makes the code more robust by preventing CMEs rather than relying on documentation to prevent them.

title: Add ability to disable plugin update checker on server startup
body:
### Feature description

Hello!

I don't want to see another useless "no new updates" log entry every server re/start.
Considering that many other plugins do the same thing, I'm sure I'm not the only one..
IMO if someone want to check for plugin update, he will be able to do this manually via command, or look at i.e. Modrinth.

I don't mind updates. I don't like it when they are forced, like Windows updates :D
Or, as in case with Grim, when we can't disable automatic checks.
IMO things like this always should be toggleable and just enabled by default.

Your consumer doesn't seem to have anything to make sure its running on the right thread and neither does this method

@ManInMyVan perhaps I'm missing something but it seems obvious to me there's an issue here. title: Add Custom Setback Violation Threshold
body:
This change introduces a configurable threshold for setbacks, allowing more flexibility in how violations are handled. It can be useful in multiple scenarios, such as integrating Grim with other anti-cheat systems like Vulcan. By delaying setbacks, more obvious cheats (e.g., flying) can be detected and handled by other systems first, preventing unnecessary interference that might limit their effectiveness.

Additionally, this feature helps reduce the impact of small false positives or minor violations on legitimate players, ensuring that occasional detection inaccuracies don’t result in unnecessary movement corrections.

The option is set to 1 by default to maintain the existing behavior, but it can be adjusted in the config for more customized handling.

body:
### Add `debugchannel` Command for Plugin Message Debugging  

#### Summary  
This PR introduces the `/grim debugchannel` command, allowing users to inspect plugin message channels received by a specified player. It is useful for debugging custom payloads, Fabric channel registration, and other client-server communication aspects.  

#### Changes  
- **New Command:** `debugchannel`  
  - Registered under `grim|grimac`  
  - Requires permission: `grim.debugchannel`  
  - Displays plugin channels a player has registered or interacted with  
- **Packet Listener:**  
  - Captures `minecraft:register` and `minecraft:unregister` messages  
  - Maintains a map of player UUIDs to registered channels  
  - Supports real-time updates and removal on player quit  
- **Localization Updates:**  
  - Added translations for `debugchannel` in all supported languages  

#### Usage  
```
/grim debugchannel <player>
```
Displays the plugin message channels registered by the specified player. If no player is provided, it defaults to the sender.  

#### Impact  
This command provides server administrators and developers with greater insight into player-client communication, aiding in debugging and cheat detection.

title: Platform Independence (future Sponge, Fabric, Neoforge, Velocity, etc... support)
body:
This PR is complete and makes Grim completely platform independent, and is a pre-requisite to adding fabric, velocity, and other platform support. It is a prelude to Grim's future where it can run everywhere and everywhere with a cross platform Check API to add external checks.

The project is now built using gradle submodules, and to add support for a new platform developers merely need to implement everything in the `ac.grim.grimac.platform.api` folder in the `common` submodule and call `GrimAPI.INSTANCE.load()` passing in an instance of `PlatformLoader`. Fabric support will be added shortly after.

title: Optimize packet event handling

labels.name: status: rebase required
labels.description: The pull request needs rebasing onto the merge branch

body:
# Optimize packet event handling

## Summary
Added efficient packet type mapping to avoid processing unnecessary checks and optimized packet event handling by only iterating over relevant handlers

I've tested basic scenarios (fly, hitboxes), but I believe this needs a thorough review before merging, as I could have inadvertently disrupted the logic of individual handlers.

## Performance improvement
I observed high CPU usage during the processing of large numbers of clientbound packets, especially during high-traffic scenarios. After implementing these optimizations, CPU consumption was significantly reduced.

The main optimization changes the packet handling mechanism to use a hashmap of packet types to handlers instead of iterating through all registered handlers for every packet. This maintains the same logical behavior while dramatically improving performance.

title: Fix copper door falses
body:
Fixes #2037

Opening copper doors is predicted by the client and they are not included in the `WOODEN_DOORS` block tag which we previously used for that. Now, I thought the issue would be fixed by just switching to the new `MOB_INTERACTABLE_DOORS` block tag. That works on all client versions where copper doors already exists, but ViaVersion translates them to Iron Doors on every version before 1.20.3, so they cannot be directly opened there. At that point, implementing all that logic in the if statement in `tickOpenable` in `CompensatedWorld` would have been too messy, so I introduced two new helper methods (`isClientSideOpenableDoor` and `isClientSideOpenableTrapdoor`) in the `Materials` class, structured similarly to the existing methods there.

I also found a condition in the existing code that would allow 1.7 players to predict opening iron doors, I tested it and it's incorrect so I removed it.

The changes were tested on a 1.21.4 server with wooden, copper and iron doors on these client versions: 1.7.10, 1.8.9, 1.20.2, 1.20.3, 1.21.4. No issues were discovered. Please let me know if I should test any other versions.

I also tested these changes on a 1.8.9 server (wooden and iron doors only) with the same client versions and found that wooden doors false when jumping into them and opening them with newer client versions even without my changes. I'll create a new issue for that.

title: Fix horse hitbox falses

labels.name: status: rebase required
labels.description: The pull request needs rebasing onto the merge branch

labels.name: status: changes requested
labels.description: Maintainers have requested changes be made to the PR before merging

body:
Fixes the hitboxes falses when mounting a horse (mentioned in #1794). When interacting with a horse, the player's rotation is forcefully set to the horse's rotation on the client in 1.13 and below so we don't receive the actual rotation used to interact with the horse, meaning we can't check for hitboxes when interacting with horses. We can still check for reach though.

This fix uses the horseInteractCausedForcedRotation field introduced in #2033 (that PR also includes a more detailed explanation of the exact cause) in the reach check to exempt only the hitbox check for horses when the player has interacted with one in the current tick (this also exempts any attacks in the same tick since these false too). For this to work, I had to move the reset of the boolean field near the end of the `onPacketReceive` method in `CheckManagerListener` so we can still access the true value in the reach check.

I have included a detailed comment in the reach check code explaining the exemption, please let me know if I should shorten that and refer here instead.

title: Memory issue with mass redstone
body:
This applies mainly to Skyblock / Survival servers, however, big redstone farms cause mass memory issues.

The following objects are mainly prevalent:

ac.grim.grimac.shaded.com.github.retrooper.packetevents.wrapper.play.server.WrapperPlayServerMultiBlockChange$EncodedBlock

ac.grim.grimac.utils.data.Pair

title: Breaking suspicious_gravel and suspicious_sand by hand will trigger FastBreak.
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

1. Place some suspicious gravel and suspicious sand, and then try to break them by hand.

Using a Shovel can allow for normal excavation.

### Grim version

grimac2.3.71
https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/actions/runs/13863014830

### Server version

1.21.4

### Client version

1.21.4

### Plugins

grimac

title: stricter duplicate handling
body:
adds a config option to
1. queue potential duplicates until the next non-async packet to check if it's actually a duplicate before processing
2. require the same position and head rotation in all duplicate packets sent in the same tick (or at least until the player rotation/position changes in a non-duplicate tick packet)

effects:
1. makes duplicate abuse impossible when paired with the other duplicate settings, with (hopefully) no issues
2. adds a negligible delay to when the server sees potential duplicate packets -- this only happens when the client sends a duplicate or is standing still turning their camera. I imagine the delay is almost always 0-5 ms in good conditions, and more in worse conditions, but it's probably unnoticeable even in those conditions -- no one will notice if it takes an additional 50 ms before the server processes one packet if the client has 200 ms ping fluctuations.
3. allows for the creation of a few new checks for verifying the legitimacy of duplicate packets:
    i. A BadPacketsJ-like check for duplicate packets
    ii. A check requiring a duplicate before every USE_ITEM

title: Fix vehicle desync when demounting too fast
body:
When demounting too quickly, a desync can occur and the player cannot move at all.
I believe the issue to be this line:
```
boolean wasInVehicle = player.getRidingVehicleId() == vehicleID;
```
The variable `wasInVehicle`  is used to determine if an entity is being mounted or dismounted. 
`player.getRidingVehicleId() ` is latency compensated. But the way `wasInVehicle ` is used it really shouldn't.

Replacing it to use `serverPlayerVehicle ` fixes the desync. Tested on 1.8.9 Server with 1.8.9 and 1.21.5 clients.
I'm not too sure if this has any other side effects.

```
[21:28:41 WARN]: [ac.grim.grimac.shaded.com.github.retrooper.packetevents.PacketEventsAPI] PacketEvents caught an unhandled exception while calling your listener.
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot read the array length because "array" is null
	at io.netty.buffer.Unpooled.wrappedBuffer(Unpooled.java:157) ~[netty-buffer-4.1.115.Final.jar:4.1.115.Final]
	at grimac-2.3.71.jar/ac.grim.grimac.shaded.io.github.retrooper.packetevents.netty.buffer.ByteBufAllocationOperatorModernImpl.wrappedBuffer(ByteBufAllocationOperatorModernImpl.java:27) ~[grimac-2.3.71.jar:?]

	at grimac-2.3.71.jar/ac.grim.grimac.shaded.com.github.retrooper.packetevents.protocol.world.chunk.reader.ChunkReader.read(ChunkReader.java:42) ~[grimac-2.3.71.jar:?]

...
```

This PR updates the `handleMapChunk` method in the `PacketWorldReaderEighteen` class to use the correct `read` method of `ChunkReader_v1_18`. For this method, an `arrayLength` argument is needed which was not required before, I copied the code to obtain this value from the PacketEvents `WrapperPlayServerChunkData` class which also uses the `read` function. With these changes, chunks seem to be read correctly again.

The `PacketWorldReaderEight` still works, apparently it requires no changes.

title: Fix cobweb 0.03 false setback
body:
Fixes #2094
When horizontally colliding with a block that has a cobweb on top and jumping into that cobweb, players are constantly being setback to a single position without any alerts, making it difficult to leave the cobweb and even impossible to move through it. The teleport is prevented by using `uncertaintyHandler.wasAffectedByStuckSpeed()` to check if the player was touching a cobweb. This fixes the issue on 1.8.

### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

**Replication**
1. join the server using the brand "\*\*my brand**"
2. have webhooks enabled and %brand% in the message content
3. flag enough to cause a webhook message to be sent

**Notes for fixing this**
- Markdown in code blocks (single or triple backticks) is not parsed and should not be escaped
- Markdown should be usable in discord.yml (don't escape all markdown in the message content, escaping all placeholder replacements should be fine)

title: WaterSpeed Legit Bypass
Enhance /grim sendalert with Hybrid MiniMessage & Legacy Formatting
body:
This PR updates the `/grim sendalert` command to support both **MiniMessage** and traditional **legacy `&` color code** formatting for staff alerts. This allows for richer alert messages using features like hover/click events and gradients, while maintaining compatibility with existing legacy formatted messages.

## Changes

*   **Input Pre-processing:**
    *   Trims whitespace and strips optional wrapping quotes (`"`/`'`) from the input message.
    *   Replaces standard `%placeholders%`.
    *   Translates legacy `&` color codes to `§` section codes. This helps the MiniMessage parser correctly interpret legacy codes embedded within MiniMessage tag attributes (e.g., `hover_text`).

*   **Hybrid Parsing Strategy:**
    1.  **MiniMessage Attempt:** The pre-processed string (with `§` codes) is first parsed using a strict `MiniMessage` instance.
        *   If MiniMessage tags are successfully processed, this result is used.
        *   If no MiniMessage tags were effectively applied (e.g., the input was pure legacy like `&cHello`), the logic proceeds to the fallback.
    2.  **Legacy/Fallback (`MessageUtil.miniMessage`):**
        *   If the MiniMessage attempt indicates the input was pure legacy/plain text, `MessageUtil.miniMessage()` is used with the original (pre-`§` translation) string to ensure correct legacy `&` code handling.
        *   If the strict MiniMessage parser encounters an exception (e.g., malformed MiniMessage or a complex mix it can't handle), `MessageUtil.miniMessage()` is used as a fallback with the original string.

This ensures pure MiniMessage, pure legacy codes, and MiniMessage containing embedded legacy codes are all handled appropriately.

## How to Test

1.  **Legacy:** `/grim sendalert &cLegacy &lAlert`
    *   _Expected:_ Colored and bolded alert.
2.  **MiniMessage:** `/grim sendalert "<red>MiniMessage <click:run_command:/say Test>Click</click>"`
    *   _Expected:_ Red text, clickable "Click".
3.  **MiniMessage with `&` in attributes:** `/grim sendalert "<hover:show_text:'&aTooltip &6Example'>Hover Me</hover>"`
    *   _Expected:_ "Hover Me" displays; hovering shows colored "Tooltip Example".
4.  **Quoted Input:** `/grim sendalert ""'<blue>Quoted MiniMessage</blue>'""`
    *   _Expected:_ Blue "Quoted MiniMessage", quotes are stripped.

This provides a robust and flexible way for staff to create alerts, without impacting any current configurations.

title: Code-Tests for simulation engine
body:
### Feature description

In the past I tried something similar to Grim (and gave up due to rounding errors and the confusing mess of MCP). Back then my project contained a custom (internal) format, which could be derived from the server itself (using a plugin) or by decoding proprietary replay sessions (we had like terabytes of data). Our goal was not to run a client and generate data, but to verify changes across a huge dataset (especially regressions leading to new false positives for already legit-verified players (sometimes myself)).

My question now, seeing this project, is whether this project actually has these automated tests? Maybe I'm just not thorough enough, but I couldn't find any way to achieve this atm. Maybe this is a design decision?

The benefits are obvious imo: Preventing (new) false positives, validating changes, reduced QA-time for iteration cycles, faster adaptation of new versions (especially seeing _where_ the differences are)
On the other hand I also completely understand the effort building something like this, the amount of data to be handled, the processing capacity needed (and the cost) as well as the question of verifiable/legit data sources (who can we trust?). One approach was to assume the minority of players are actually cheaters and verify against the whole dataset while looking on the shift in alerts while checking some new or now missing alerts. The amount of data fortunately wasn't a problem for us back then, but maybe today it may be (depending on your connections to big networks and the prevalence of "silent cheats" today; we had multiple terabytes of replay sessions per month 😅 ).

title: False positives when generic.attackDamage is set to 0.0
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

For 1.8 PVP-focused servers, owners might decide to disable "clientside knockback reducing". This is done by setting the `generic.attackDamage` to 0.0 on the client side only. This way, the client does not consider an attack an attack. It still sends ENTITY_ATTACK to the server, but the motion as well as the sprinting state will be kept on the client.

This is how to do it from the server:
```java
PacketPlayOutUpdateAttributes packet = new PacketPlayOutUpdateAttributes(sender.getEntityId(), List.of());
attributesField.set(packet, List.of(packet.new AttributeSnapshot("generic.attackDamage", 0.0f, List.of())));
((CraftPlayer) sender).getHandle().playerConnection.sendPacket(packet);
```
But doing so makes the Grim prediction engine to freak out.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d99f04f-26e5-4264-b5dd-d14f64c31096)

To fix that, the attack slow must only be applied when the value is > 0.0 on the client.
https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/blob/984cfeecbe9e214d62b218706114bd265f1bf3db/common/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/predictionengine/predictions/PredictionEngine.java#L416

### Grim version

984cfeecbe9e214d62b218706114bd265f1bf3db

### Server version

1.8 paper.  But should be the same on any.

### Client version

Any

Custom

title: Add /grim history
body:
After extensive testing in LightningGrim. I believe grim history is ready for usage upstream. The only flaws that came up in prod testing were 
1. Inefficiencies at scale (already addressed with an explanation below)
2. Online player username's not autocompleting, which has since been patched (but in a somewhat inefficient way I will address another time)
3. Missing placeholders for %grim_version% %client_brand% %client_version% %server_version% as options

The database system has been refactored to use unique table names and a storage system that is more complex but efficient at large scales, deduplicating strings and using 16 bytes instead of 36 to store UUIDS.

Backwards compatibility has not been kept with historically formatted data. Using the new /grim history will result in none of the data being migrated (though the command will remain functional, nothing will break, and it is highly unlikely the storage format will be changed again).

title: Possible fase positive
body: ### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it tl;dr Not sure if this is a false positive, a player flags Grim a lot but we don't see him cheating. I am sorry for the unconventional report and understand that this is not a priority but if you have free time I would really appreciate the help. We are on 1.21.7 Leaf server, we use ViaVersion and Geyser but this issue is about a 1.21.7 player so I am not sure how it could affect but I tell you just in case. There is a player that keeps triggering Grim, our first suspicion was that he was cheating so we have spied him on Vanish for a very very long time and seen replays of him with AnticheatReplay, he never looked different from any other player. I was seeing him when I took this screenshot and nothing looked strange, here are a few logs in case it helps: https://paste.grim.ac/dxGz0m8 https://paste.grim.ac/AtcbhGy https://paste.grim.ac/ILSHNFE My question is mostly a: "Is there any way for this to happen to a legit user or should we trust the flags and ban him?" We had some false flags but never that many, I am sorry for the inconveniences and if I can submit any other thing please tell me. I am a bit new to this so I am sorry if this is like a huge facepalm for you guys, thanks for the help. ### Grim Log https://paste.grim.ac/dxGz0m8 ### Server version ### Client version fabric 1.21.7 ### Plugins

title: Periodic permission checks
body:
### Feature description

I'm managing a server with several worlds (overworld, challenge, real_world, etc.) and want to only apply anti cheat to specific world (e.g. challenge_world_1).

I tried to set `grim.exempt` to true with context world=world, world=world_nether ... in Luckperms -- didn't work.

After using `/lp verbose on grim`, I discovered that `grim.exempt` is only checked once, after a player joins.

Add check period (e.g. 1000ms) can solve it.

How to reproduce:

1. Join world = world(grim.exempt=true), `/mv tp challenge_world_1` (grim.exempt=false) -- Player can cheat in challenge_world_1!
2. Join world = challenge_world_1, `/mv tp world` -- Player can't cheat in overworld!

Expected behavior: `world` can cheat & `challenge_world_1` can't cheat.

title: CrashH falses with long commands
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

1. Place a command block
2. Enter a valid command that is 257 characters or longer (`help ` followed by any 252 characters for example)
3. Flag every time the cursor moves
The issue is this check assumes that tab completions can only be up to 256 characters, since chat can only contain 256 characters. This is not true, because command blocks use tab completions and can contain up to 32500 characters.

title: WorldGuard clickable flag option triggers ChatB violation with GrimAntiCheat
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

When using the WorldGuard command `/rg flags`, there is a clickable option "Click to unset".  
Clicking this option does nothing, and after repeatedly clicking it, GrimAntiCheat begins to trigger violations.  

For example, it displays messages like:  
`TheLittle_Yang triggered ChatB (x10) command=/rg flag -w "world" -h 1 __global__ ride`

1. Run `/rg flags` on a region managed by WorldGuard.  
2. In chat, click the "Click to unset" option for a flag.  
3. Nothing happens.
4. If you keep clicking, Grim starts flagging with ChatB violations about command execution.

This makes WorldGuard's clickable flag editing unusable when Grim is enabled.

title: ChatB (formerly ExploitC) can false
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

Requires 1.8 server, viaversion, viachatfixer, and a modern client.

Newer versions are able to send longer messages, however due to protocol stuff viaversion will cut the message to the intended size (which later viachatfixer will recover), however if the last char of such cut message ends in a space, ChatB (formerly ExploitC) will flag it as it being an invalid chat message since it checks if `message.trim() != message`, which wont be true for this trimmed message if the last char is a space.

A way to replicate this is with a message that is spaces and some other char repeated, that way its a 50/50 chance of a space hitting the 120th position or whatever it was. If it sends fine, just add/remove a char from the start and try again, one of the two cases will fail.

eg:
`/a hello . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .`
will send fine but
`/a helloo . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .`
will get flagged and removed

### Grim version

c2a07bd (but has been happening for a while now)

### Server version

1.8 sportpaper, but should happen in any 1.8 server software

### Client version

1.21.8, but will work with any version that allows longer chat messages

### Plugins

Viaversion and viachatfixer are needed to test the functionality

title: Placing blocks on arrows sets you back
body: ### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it I believe grim thinks placing blocks inside entities is illegal, and so considers the block not to have placed for simulation purposes. This is not the case for thrown arrow entities stuck in blocks or dropped item entities (this last one was fixed already). This can cause setbacks or weird movement as grim teleports you down etc. Note: brief testing shows marker armorstands may have this issue too, and (not tested) area effect clouds, paintings, itemframes etc are another entity that comes to mind that can be built over. 1. Place arrows on the ground, preferably with infinity so you won't pick them up 2. Try to jump and place a block where the arrow is 3. Get slightly desynced and teleported down as if simulation thought the block place was illegalNote: a plugin that denies the block places may help https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f5e9213-1787-4ca3-af58-bb547dbde31b Grim verbose: ### Grim Log N/A ### Server version 1.8 sportpaper (I don't believe it is necessary to reproduce) ### Client version 1.21.8, but i believe this is not relevant ### Plugins Viaversion, viabackwards, viarewind, (I don't believe they are necessary to reproduce)
