body:
### Stack trace

No stack trace

### How to replicate it if known

1. Run Grim on SportPaper 1.8.8, or possibly any 1.8.8 server
2. Have a noticeable amount of players online with all non-experimental checks enabled
3. Eventually, `disconnect.timeout` spam will happen in console. Some players will be shown in `/grim player list` as offline if they are not connected to the server when they typically would not show in this list at all. Some players will have the `disconnect.timeout` spammed as kicking them but they will still be connected to the server.
4. Eventually, certain players may not be able to log onto the server. There is no observed trend as to who is and isn't able to connect (specific versions or otherwise do not seem to have been unable to connect more than others).

title: PacketOrderP impacting chunk loading speed
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

- Setup server with render distance 10, simulation distance 6 (not sure if relevant).
- Make sure experimental checks are disabled
- Teleport to an area where chunks are already generated, preferably loaded as well but I saw no difference.

Notice how slowly chunks take to show.

I did a git bisect to find where it started: `bbab7e222c294956959d6ede9a53f8011ad3ecf7`

I added the same conditional code that is used on `flag()` to the top of `onPacketReceive` and `onPacketSend`
``` 
if (player.disableGrim || (experimental && !player.isExperimentalChecks()) || exemptPermission)
            return false;
```

Repeating the steps above chunks load quicker.


Even though the check is experimental, it still runs the events, `onPacketReceive` does not do much since it's experimental `flagAndAlert` instantly returns, `onPacketSend` however always does something even when experimental checks are disabled.


Proposed solution:
- Before calling the event handlers on `CheckManager` check if it is experimental or not and if the player has experimental checks enabled, don't call the handlers if not enabled.



Somewhat related but not directly:

I noticed the same behavior happens with checks that are not enabled, even though they don't flag, some still take action, documentation is not very explicit that this can happen, my expectation as a user is that if I disable a check it does not do anything at all, an example of this is `Reach` there is `cancelImpossibleHits` to partially prevent it from taking action, but if it's considered `tooManyAttacks` it will still cancel the action, again my expectation is that the check doesn't do anything at all if disabled, not needing an extra configuration to prevent it from doing something.

title: Remove GrimAPI.detectPlatform()
body:
### Feature description

To implement my platform without modifying the common module, I have to rely on workarounds and explicitly set `Platform.BUKKIT`. I suggest changing `Platform` from an enum to an interface, and determining the platform not through `detectPlatform()`, but by explicitly specifying it in the `PlatformLoader`.

title: More setback customizability
body:
### Feature description

Hello, I thought it would be helpful if Grim had more ways to customize the behavior of Simulation setbacks. It might benefit certain server developers as they could have more control over them.

I found a video of some velocity-correcting mitigation (which seems to work in a slightly different way than how Grim does by default), the server was running Polar:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b91614b-397d-4937-83b8-b508f6b6bf62

Just thought this would be a decent addition.

title: Fix gamemode change on dimension change bug for spectate command
body: This issue happened when using the spectate command on a player in another dimension. the spectator was set to survival mode. Now simply checks that the player is not just changing dimensions before changing gamemode.

title: Fix spectate command resetting gamemode when spectating someone in another dimension
body: This issue happened when using the spectate command on a player in another dimension. the spectator was set to survival mode. Now checks that the player is not spectating before changing gamemode.

title: feat: support for postgresql
body:
I added a PostgreSQL implementation for handling violations.
The changes have been tested against the latest Fabric releases.

When someone needs this, just apply these configuration changes:
```yaml
history:
    enabled: true
    ...
    database:
        # Use SQLITE for local storage, use MYSQL if you have an external MySQL database. This is only updated on server restart
        type: POSTGRESQL
        # MySQL connection details
        ...
```

title: feat: add support for offline player history
body:
I added a player database for the history command to improve multi-server support (and fabric offline support).
The player information is now updated on both join and quit events.

This primarily benefits cases where a player is reported from another server, allowing us to retrieve his user data.

Database structure:
```sql
TABLE grim_history_players (
    uuid BINARY(16) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY, 
    name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
    last_seen BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() * 1000)
);
```

Update logic:
```sql
INSERT INTO grim_history_players
    (uuid, name, last_seen)
    VALUES (?, ?, ?)
    ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE 
        name = VALUES(name),
        last_seen = VALUES(last_seen)
```

Methods:
```java
void updateHistoryPlayer(GrimPlayer player)

Optional<HistoryPlayer> getHistoryPlayer(UUID uuid)
Optional<HistoryPlayer> getHistoryPlayer(String playerName)
```

Tested with sqlite and mysql on latest fabric version.

Update:
While reviewing the mysql implementation, I discovered an issue with ``CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS``. I resolved it by first checking for existing indexes and creating them only when they don't already exist.

title: MultiActionsC/D false with server-opened GUIs
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

1. Have a plugin that opens a server-side GUI in some way
2. Time your inventory close to be right when the inventory opens.
3. Observe MultiActionsD false

Video: https://youtu.be/_ZCZQZQtwlM

For MultiActionsC, do the same but with spam left clicking (to click a slot right when it opens). It is harder to reproduce this than MultiActionD. This seems to happen more often for delayed environments. I was unable to reproduce a MultiActionsC false on a local server, but was able to on a remote server at 20-30ms.

### Grim version

2.3.73-2d785fd+lite

### Server version

Paper version 1.21.8-60-main@29c8822

### Client version

Tested on 1.21.8 & 1.21.10 vanilla

### Plugins/Mods

GrimAC, packetevents, TestPlugin
(TestPlugin is for opening a server GUI)

title: feat: add breakpoint-tolerant clock system and refactor GrimPlayer time handling
body:
This commit Implement zero-cost breakpoint-tolerant time tracking.

It introduces a new time architecture for GrimPlayer that allows developers to pause execution at breakpoints without triggering Timer, FastBreak, or Velocity violations upon resumption.

Changes:
- Refactored `GrimPlayer` to use `nano()`/`now()` overrides instead of direct System calls.
- Added `DebugGrimPlayer` subclass which uses `ThreadLocal` to track intra-packet execution time.
- Logic automatically absorbs execution pauses >200ms (breakpoints) while correctly preserving inter-packet delays (server lag/AFK).
- Added `processingPacket()` hooks to the Packet Dispatcher and Tick Manager to manage thread-local timers.
- Performance impact is 0 in production due to JIT monomorphic inlining and dead code elimination of the base class methods.

title: Optimize LatencyUtils: concurrent, autoboxing
body:
ConcurrentLinkedQueue is particularly suitable for this scenario. Changes to the queue are atomic, so it's thread-safe.

This change has not actually been tested, but should be much faster than the synchronized blocks, especially when add the tasks.

Additionally, Changed Pair to record class. Using Pair will autoboxing the ints, it's an unnecessary cost.

title: ci: make runner configurable to work around Tenki issues
body:
Tenki's self-hosted runners started failing on Dec 19, 2025 with
"Invalid URL" errors during artifact upload. This adds a configurable
runner input to all workflows, allowing easy switching between
GitHub-hosted and Tenki runners.

- Add `runner` input to reusable build workflow (default: ubuntu-latest)
- Expose runner option in gradle-publish.yml for manual runs  
- Explicitly set runner in release.yml
- Bump upload-artifact v4 → v6

title: Add gamemode and item checks to AirLiquidBreak to prevent false flags.
body:
In current build of Grim, the anti cheat would falsely flag users in creative mode who attack/attempt to break a block with items that cannot break blocks in creative mode. Items like swords, debug sticks, maces and tridents. This patch skips the checks for users in spectator mode and users in creative mode who have those items held.
Tested on private server on 1.21.4 with Grim while on a 1.21.11 fabric client.

title: Piston parity on Fabric with Bukkit
body:
@runningbird2 has volunteered to take this one.  AFAIK this is the current state

https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/compare/2.0...runningbird2:Grim:feature/fabric-piston-event#diff-eadb1090dd3472159a54d320b159f6dafe051b38452b5a033900e404e5ac9426

I've already given it a quick review on the Discord, but as a reminder:
- There should already be a method to map the directions, if there isn't make a util similar to ones that exist instead of putting it in the piston handler class
- Deduplicate with the handling of the code from Bukkit Version and optimize (see how I do it in Lightning Grim more efficiently: https://github.com/Axionize/LightningGrim/blob/lightning/bukkit/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/platform/bukkit/events/PistonEvent.java). Make the distance check use primitives so it can be crossplatform and not use vectors.

- Add support our entire range of Fabric versions (1.16.1 to 1.21.11)

title: Fix Discord Webhook PAPI Placeholders + Update default Discord config and translations.
body:
### Summary
This PR fixes issues with PAPI placeholders not being parsed in Discord webhooks. It also overhauls the Discord webhook system to improve formatting and standardize localization across all supported languages.

*   **Formatting**:
    *   Implemented context-aware Markdown escaping in `MessageUtil`.
    *   If a placeholder is wrapped in backticks (e.g., `` `%player%` ``), only backticks and backslashes are escaped to preserve the raw look.
    *   If a placeholder is in plain text, it is aggressively filtered to prevent users from breaking embed formatting (e.g., using underscores or asterisks).
*   **Configuration & Localization**:
    *   Updated **all** language files to wrap user-controlled variables (`%player%`, `%brand%`) in backticks by default.
    *   Reordering the default order of information in embeds across all languages (Player -> Brand -> Check -> Data).
    *   Fixed translation errors:
        *   **Chinese:** Changed "Server lag degree" to "TPS" and "Violation Rate" to "Count".
        *   **Italian:** Changed "Cheats Detected" to "Check" (Controllo).
        *   **French/Dutch/Turkish:** Improved terminology for "Brand".

title: Setback breaks player rotation when modern client (1.21+) is riding a vehicle on 1.8 servers
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

When running Grim on a 1.8 server, a player using a modern client (1.21+) experiences completely broken rotation while riding a vehicle if a setback is triggered.

This results in severe position / rotation desync and makes the player unable to look around correctly.

### **REPRODUCTION STEP**
1) Create a 1.8 server and join using a 1.21+ client (via ViaVersion)
2) Enter a vehicle and trigger a server teleport (being more than 4 blocks away from the player’s last known position)
3) Move the camera (yaw / pitch) on the affected player
4) Join with a second player or print bukkit yaw / pitch and observe that the player’s rotation remains frozen from the server’s perspective

### **TECHNICAL DETAILS**
Grim’s setback logic assumes that a `PlayerPositionLook` teleport sent by the server is always applied by the client and confirmed via a matching `PositionLook` packet.
This assumption breaks for modern clients when the player is riding a vehicle:

In the 1.8 client, even when the player is riding a vehicle, the server-sent `PlayerPositionLook` is applied directly to the player entity.

In modern clients, when the player is a passenger, the teleport positions in `PlayerPositionLook` are discarded. Instead, the client responds with a `PositionLook` packet containing the last known valid player position from before entering the vehicle, rather than the teleport position.

Grim compares the teleport position sent by the server with the position returned by the client to confirm the setback. Since the modern client never applies the teleport, the returned position will never match the teleport position.

As a result, the setback is never confirmed, causing subsequent movement and rotation packets to be canceled, which leads to desynchronized rotation.

### **VIDEO**
https://youtu.be/AUoDu3ibofg

### Grim version

2.3.73-14573da

### Server version

Spigot / Paper 1.8.8

### Affected Platform(s)

Bukkit

### Plugins/Mods

Grim, ViaVersion and a custom plugin to set the passenger player to a distance greater than 4 blocks

title: Project Codex - Config / Settings API
Velocity + GrimAC: one player times out when two players connect from the same IP (NAT), Folia 1.21.11
body:
### Stack trace

No stack trace is produced. The disconnect is a clean timeout, not an exception or crash.

Backend log shows only:

`<player> lost connection: Timed out
`
Velocity log shows:

```
[connected player] <player> (/xxxxxxxxxxxxx) has disconnected: An internal error occurred in your connection.
[connected player] <player> (/xxxxxxxxxxxxx): read timed out
```

GrimAC does not print any error, exception, or stack trace at the moment of the disconnect.

With debug-pipeline-on-join: true enabled, the Netty pipeline is printed correctly and is identical for both players.

This appears to be a keepalive / packet stall, not an exception-based failure.

### How to replicate it if known

You can reliably reproduce this issue with the following setup:

1. Set up a Velocity proxy with:
- player-info-forwarding-mode = modern
- Proper forwarding secret

2. Set up a Folia backend (1.21.11-10) with:
- Velocity forwarding enabled
- GrimAC installed and enabled

3. Ensure both players connect from the same public IP (same NAT / same network).

4. Steps:
- Player A connects through Velocity → backend
- Player B connects through Velocity → backend (same IP)
- Both players successfully join the server

5. Wait ~30–40 seconds.

6. Result:
- One of the players (always only one) is disconnected with:

`Timed out
`

- The other player remains connected normally.

Control tests (to confirm behavior):

- Remove GrimAC → issue no longer occurs
- Remove Velocity (connect directly to backend) → issue no longer occurs
- Connect players from different IPs → issue no longer occurs

title: Fast Break triggers after equipping a tool via Shulker Box GUI

### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

A Fast Break false positive occurs when a player opens a Shulker Box with an empty hand, equips a tool within the GUI, and immediately breaks a block. The anti-cheat/plugin seems to calculate the mining speed based on the previously empty hand rather than the newly equipped tool.

https://youtu.be/KQBpDS5FWIk

To Replicate:
1. Ensure your main hand is empty.
2. Place and open a Shulker Box.
3. Inside the Shulker Box GUI (or Inventory view), move a tool (e.g., Pickaxe) into your active hotbar slot.
4. Close the GUI.
5. Immediately attempt to break a block with the tool.

title: ExploitB breaks vanilla books
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

Step 1: Acquire book and quill
Step 2: Begin writing a book with right click or whatever you have Use Item/Place Block bound to.
Step 2: Hold down the period key until the entire page if full
Step 3: Click "Sign"
Step 4: Enter "Test" as a name
Step 5: Click "Sign and Close"

The book fails to sign and all changes are reverted. Verbose logging reports "Exploit B" - "page too long" 

Further testing shows the check starts failing at 261 characters, despite vanilla allowing for 798. So this check is extremely inaccurate for what's possible in vanilla. This has wasted many cumulative hours for legitimate players when their work gets erased due to using a few too many punctuation characters. At the very least this check should not be failing for standard ascii characters written on a standard keyboard in vanilla.

title: BadPacketsJ false positive when standing still and right-clicking on 1.21+
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

## Description
BadPacketsJ incorrectly flags players who stand completely still and right-click items in the air.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Join a 1.21+ server with Grim installed
2. Stand completely still (no movement, no mouse movement)
3. Hold any item or empty hand
4. Right-click repeatedly in the air
5. Get flagged by BadPacketsJ

## Expected behavior
No flag - the player is not cheating

## Actual behavior
BadPacketsJ flags with "Rotation in use item packet did not match tick rotation"

## Root cause analysis
In `BadPacketsJ.java` line 43-48, float values are compared using `==`:

```java
if (rotation.yaw() == player.yaw && rotation.pitch() == player.pitch) {
    continue;
}
flagAndAlert();
Float comparison with == fails due to floating-point precision issues, even when values are essentially identical.
Suggested fix
Use epsilon comparison:
java
private static final float EPSILON = 0.001f;

if (Math.abs(rotation.yaw() - player.yaw) < EPSILON 
    && Math.abs(rotation.pitch() - player.pitch) < EPSILON) {
    continue;
}

### Grim version

Grim-2.3.73-b7a719d

### Server version

mc.loyisa.cn latest

### Client version

1.21.4

### Plugins/Mods

mc.loyisa.cn latest

title: grim.nomodifypacket.checkname permissions have no effect
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

Use `grim.nomodifypacket.checkname` permissions on a check for example`grim.nomodifypacket.fastbreak`.

Use fastbreak or speed mine and observe packet canceling instead of just alerts as intended.

Note: The nosetback permission does appear to be respected by many checks, but not by all (presumably this is intended). this issue is for nomodifypacket only.

grimac-fabric-2.3.73-f95d877.jar

title: fix(Phase): exempt shulker box lid push from phase detection
body:
Fix proposal for #2431 

When a player stands on an open shulker box under a low ceiling, the opening lid pushes the player into the ceiling block.
Phase prediction incorrectly flags this as a phase-through because newBB intersected a block that oldBB did not.
The same false positive occurs on the rebound when the player briefly clips back into the shulker's own base block.

This PR adds `isShulkerPushedIntoBlock()` which exempts the flag only when both the player's new bounding box AND the offending block are inside the shulker's push zone (1x1x1 base + one block in the facing direction).

Requiring the offending block to also be inside the push zone prevents bypasses where the player stands near a shulker and noclips into adjacent blocks unrelated to the lid.

title: fix(fabric): guard replaceNativePlayer cache miss
body:
## Summary
Add a null guard in Fabric `replaceNativePlayer` to prevent a hard NPE when the platform player cache entry is missing during `ServerPlayer.restoreFrom`.

## Problem
On Fabric, Grim currently assumes a cached `PlatformPlayer` always exists when `ServerPlayerMixin` fires at `restoreFrom` tail.

When that assumption is violated, this call chain crashes:
- `ServerPlayerMixin#onRestoreFrom` -> `FabricPlatformPlayerFactory#replaceNativePlayer`
- `cache.getPlayer(uuid)` returns `null`
- direct dereference throws NPE

This manifests as `Ticking player` packet handling failures and `Internal server error` disconnects.

## Root Cause
`FabricPlatformPlayerFactory.replaceNativePlayer` dereferences `cache.getPlayer(uuid)` without checking for null, but lifecycle timing can produce legitimate cache misses (for example around disconnect/invalidation vs reconstruction timing).

## Changes
- File: `fabric/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/platform/fabric/player/FabricPlatformPlayerFactory.java`
- Method: `replaceNativePlayer(@NotNull UUID uuid, @NotNull ServerPlayer serverPlayerEntity)`
- Change: guard `cache.getPlayer(uuid)` and only call `replaceNativePlayer(...)` when a cached entry exists.

## Validation
- Deployed test build in a Fabric 1.21.11 environment where this stack had been observed.
- Server startup was healthy; no `PlatformPlayerCache.getPlayer(...)` / `replaceNativePlayer` NPEs seen after deployment.


## Related
- Closes #2508

title: NullPointerException spam: player.dimensionType is null on 1.16.5
body:
**Bug Report: NullPointerException on player.dimensionType after any teleportation causing movement issues**

**Description:**
After any kind of player teleportation (duel arena TP, RTP in the overworld, etc.), GrimAC starts spamming a NullPointerException in the console, and the teleported players are unable to sprint, though jumping still works fine.

**Error:**
```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "ac.grim.grimac.shaded.com.github.retrooper.packetevents.protocol.world.dimension.DimensionType.isUltraWarm()" because "player.dimensionType" is null
  at ac.grim.grimac.predictionengine.PlayerBaseTick.updateInWaterStateAndDoFluidPushing(PlayerBaseTick.java:145)
  at ac.grim.grimac.predictionengine.PlayerBaseTick.doBaseTick(PlayerBaseTick.java:57)
  at ac.grim.grimac.predictionengine.MovementCheckRunner.check(MovementCheckRunner.java:501)
  ...
```

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Teleport a player using any method — duel arena teleport OR random teleport (RTP) in the overworld
2. GrimAC immediately starts spamming NullPointerException in the console
3. The teleported player is unable to sprint, but can still jump normally

**Actual Behavior:**
- Console is spammed with NullPointerException on every movement packet
- GrimAC fails to correctly process the player's movement state after teleport
- Sprint is blocked as suspicious movement, while jumping passes the checks fine
- This happens across multiple teleport types, not just duel arenas

**Suspected Root Cause:**
After any teleportation, `player.dimensionType` is not initialized in time (or not initialized at all), causing GrimAC's movement checks to crash when attempting to call `DimensionType.isUltraWarm()`. This appears to be a general issue with how GrimAC handles post-teleport state, not specific to any one plugin.

**Environment:**
- Server: ShieldSpigot 1.16.5
- GrimAC version: 2.3.73-4ca65b1
- PacketEvents version: 2.11.2

**Additional Notes:**
Both issues (console spam and sprint being blocked) are directly linked — fixing the NPE should resolve the movement problem as well. The bug is reproducible with at least two different teleport plugins (Duels plugin and RTP plugin), suggesting the root cause is inside GrimAC itself.

title: Reach/Hitboxes false when delayed swapping from non-ranged item to ranged item
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

1. Get a ranged weapon. e.g. `/give @s wooden_sword[attack_range={max_reach:5.0,hitbox_margin:0.0}]`
2. Swap to a non-ranged item.
3. Swap to the ranged item, then *one tick later*, attack.
4. Observe false.

Demonstration Video: https://youtu.be/mVcnRR7UIKg

This is caused by the fact that the item held swapping (non-ranged -> ranged) is not broadcasted to the server until the start of the next client tick. Because of this, even after a tick of waiting (which allows the usage of the ranged component), Grim reads the incorrect start-of-tick item.

~~It is worth to note that spears are not affected as they do not attack using the client-side calculations. Only custom items with `attack_range` set are affected.~~

title: Reach false due to additional reach granted by movement from attack_range
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

1. Give yourself a ranged weapon. e.g. `/give @s wooden_sword[attack_range={max_reach:5.0,hitbox_margin:0.0}]`
2. Stand & aim just slightly out of range of an entity.
3. Attack while swapping to a non-ranged weapon.
4. Observe reach false.

Demonstration Video: https://youtu.be/gpwchmenUCU

Note: This "additional reach" effect is amplified the faster the player is moving. However, it also affects stationary players (as shown in video) due to the fact that gravity is reflected on the `Player#getKnownMovement()` call, which is used to calculate the additional reach.

This is caused by the crosshair target being calculated differently than normal when using an `attack_range` component item. This calculation additionally adds a small amount of reach based on the dot product between the known movement call and the look position. This usually does not affect ranged weapons by itself due to an additional check (the normal one) being made when the attack happens. However, when the attribute swapping happens, no checks are made as there is no `attack_range` component.

This false affects spears.

title: Allow custom domains for Discord webhooks
body:
### Feature description

Currently, in common/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/manager/DiscordManager.java (Line 32), the WEBHOOK_REGEX strictly enforces that the webhook URL must start with https://discord.com/api.

```Java
private static final Predicate<String> WEBHOOK_REGEX = Pattern.compile("^https://discord\\.com/api(?:/v\\d+)?/webhooks/\\d+/[\\w-]+(\\?thread_id=\\d+)?$").asMatchPredicate();
```
This strict domain-level validation prevents users from using:

Webhook Proxies: While issue #734 previously addressed proxy support, the current WEBHOOK_REGEX enforces the discord.com domain, which effectively breaks or prevents routing traffic through custom proxy URLs again.

Compatible API Endpoints: Self-hosted or middleware solutions that provide Discord-compatible API structures cannot be used if they are hosted on different domains.

Proposed Solution
I would like to have more flexibility in configuring the webhook URL to support diverse networking requirements. Specifically, the validation could be loosened to ensure the URL remains a valid https endpoint without strictly enforcing the discord.com domain, or a configuration toggle (e.g., disable-webhook-validation: true) could be added to allow advanced users to bypass this regex check when using custom API endpoints or proxies.

title: Added a new experimental checks `ConnectionA-B`
body: The check samples transaction ping values using an EvictingQueue and analyzes their average over a fixed window. If the average ping exceeds the configured threshold, a buffer is increased and the player may be flagged after repeated violations. Key features: - Uses EvictingQueue to collect ping samples - Calculates average delay via GrimMath - Buffer-based violation system to reduce false positives - Ignores players during teleport, join grace period, or while in vehicles - Optional setback execution on violation This check is currently marked as experimental and may be tuned further based on live testing. No AI was used.

title: Fast break false in nether when item is received while being in an inventory window
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

1. Open a chest inventory and stay there
2. Give to that player an iron pickaxe via give command (apparently happens with all tools)
3. Close a chest inventory
4. Try to break a block using received pickaxe, most luckily it will trigger a fast break

It doesn't happen reliably. Sometimes it doesn't false fast break, sometimes it falses for some time only.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/842628cb-758e-440e-87a0-2ca415477a3c

It also happens with inventory windows created by plugins and items given via `player.inventory.addItem` Bukkit API (that's how I originally discovered it).

I tried to investigate this and apparently here in [FastBreak.onPacketReceive](https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/blob/f0e15b05210c5815376e5d043b5e54fd7b7f176e/common/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/checks/impl/breaking/FastBreak.java#L121) next call to `player.inventory.getHeldItem()` returns an empty stack. Basically when I get a fast break false, it's because Grim thinks I hold nothing in my hand. 
Here in SET_SLOT listener [this callback](https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/blob/f0e15b05210c5815376e5d043b5e54fd7b7f176e/common/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/utils/latency/CompensatedInventory.java#L479) never executes because `isPacketInventoryActive == false` in that case.

### Grim version

2.3.74-bf10e23

### Server version

1.21.11

No mods on client or plugins on a server.
Full default settings of Paper and Grim.

title: feat: Fabric 26.1 official namespace support
body:
## Summary

This PR finalizes Fabric 26.1 official-namespace support and brings the branch in line with the validated fork state, including reproducible dependency pinning and multi-platform startup harness coverage.

In addition to the original 26.1 migration work, this update adds end-to-end Grim + PacketEvents test harnesses for Fabric and Bukkit startup validation and documents exact reproduction steps.

## Alignment with Axionize architecture guidance

This branch now explicitly follows Axionize’s guidance:

1) **Defaults remain stable**
- Default builds do not rely on local-only artifact behavior.
- Local overrides are opt-in via `-PmavenLocalOverride=true` / `MAVEN_LOCAL_OVERRIDE=true`.

2) **Reproducible dependency coordinates**
- PacketEvents is pinned to an exact snapshot git coordinate.
- cloud-fabric is pinned to an exact unique snapshot coordinate (instead of floating `-SNAPSHOT`).

3) **Deterministic resolution behavior**
- Repository strategy and docs are aligned to reproducible defaults and explicit local override workflows.

## What was added/updated in the final iteration

- Added and hardened Grim + PacketEvents harness scripts under `tests/scripts`:
  - Fabric official 26.1 bootstrap/startup flow
  - Bukkit Paper 1.20.6 startup flow
  - Bukkit Spigot 1.21.1 startup flow
  - Full-stack runner for combined coverage

- Improved harness reliability:
  - Correct PacketEvents main-jar selection logic
  - Deterministic timeout/log capture handling
  - Optional `SKIP_CLEAN=true` for faster local iteration without changing CI-safe defaults

- Applied remaining safe cleanup/follow-up fixes in Fabric adapters and docs.

## Proof of tested compatibility

Latest smoke run validated Grim + the restructured PacketEvents build together:

- **Fabric 26.1 (official namespace):**
  - Ran bootstrap + startup harness with Java 25.
  - Observed successful startup marker: `Done (...)`.
  - Grim and PacketEvents both initialized in server logs.

- **Bukkit Paper 1.20.6 (older-version path):**
  - Ran `run-all-grim-pe-bukkit-harnesses.sh` case 1/2.
  - Observed successful startup marker: `Done (14.895s)!`.

- **Bukkit Spigot 1.21.1:**
  - Ran `run-all-grim-pe-bukkit-harnesses.sh` case 2/2.
  - Observed successful startup marker: `Done (14.791s)!`.

This demonstrates the current changes do not regress the tested older Bukkit compatibility path while enabling Fabric 26.1.

## Reproduction / How to run

### 1) Fabric 26.1 official namespace (primary target)
- `./tests/scripts/bootstrap-grim-pe-official-261.sh`
- `./tests/scripts/run-server.sh --server-dir tests/runs/grim-pe-26.1 --java-bin /path/to/java25`

### 2) Bukkit Paper 1.20.6 startup validation
- `./tests/scripts/bootstrap-grim-pe-bukkit-paper-1206.sh`
- `./tests/scripts/run-bukkit-server.sh --server-dir tests/runs/grim-pe-paper-1.20.6`

### 3) Bukkit Spigot 1.21.1 startup validation
- `./tests/scripts/bootstrap-grim-pe-bukkit-spigot-1211.sh`
- `./tests/scripts/run-bukkit-server.sh --server-dir tests/runs/grim-pe-spigot-1.21.1`

### 4) One-command harness runs
- `./tests/scripts/run-all-grim-pe-harnesses.sh`
- `./tests/scripts/run-all-grim-pe-bukkit-harnesses.sh`
- `./tests/scripts/run-all-grim-pe-stack-harnesses.sh`

## What still needs testing

To further strengthen confidence before merge, remaining coverage should include:

- Additional Fabric intermediary compatibility runs (for selected non-26.1 versions).
- More Bukkit versions (at least one additional Paper and Spigot target each).
- Basic join/playflow checks (not only startup) for each harnessed platform.
- Regression checks for representative ViaVersion/pre-Via user paths in real server stacks.

## Validation status

- `./gradlew :fabric:compileJava` passes on the updated branch.
- Harness scripts pass shell syntax checks.
- Startup coverage now includes:
  - Fabric 26.1 official path
  - Older-version Bukkit path (Paper 1.20.6)
  - Spigot 1.21.1 path

## Notes

- Fabric module target remains MC 26.1 official namespace.
- Bukkit harnesses are startup compatibility checks for cross-stack confidence.
- This update is intended to be a clean, reproducible, maintainer-friendly finalization of the PR branch.

title: fix: accept set_camera packet alias in camera compensation
body:
## Summary
- update `CompensatedCameraEntity` packet gate to accept both `PacketType.Play.Server.CAMERA` and `PacketType.Play.Server.SET_CAMERA`
- keep existing `WrapperPlayServerCamera` parsing and compensation flow unchanged
- reason: 26.1 protocol naming uses `set_camera` in Mojang's packet registry/class names, while existing integrations may still surface `CAMERA`

## Evidence from decompiled 26.1 server source
From local decompile at `/root/decompiled-minecraft/server-26.1-src`:

1) Packet registry includes `set_camera`:
`net/minecraft/network/protocol/game/GamePacketTypes.java`
```java
public static final PacketType<ClientboundSetCameraPacket> CLIENTBOUND_SET_CAMERA = GamePacketTypes.createClientbound("set_camera");
```

2) Dedicated packet class is `ClientboundSetCameraPacket` and its type points to `CLIENTBOUND_SET_CAMERA`:
`net/minecraft/network/protocol/game/ClientboundSetCameraPacket.java`
```java
@Override
public PacketType<ClientboundSetCameraPacket> type() {
    return GamePacketTypes.CLIENTBOUND_SET_CAMERA;
}
```

## Test plan
- [x] verified by spectate flow, camera packet observed and parsed

title: Require external PacketEvents for Bukkit builds
body:
## Summary
- switch the Bukkit release artifact to depend on the standalone `packetevents` plugin instead of bundling a second PacketEvents copy
- keep PacketEvents shaded for non-Bukkit modules while excluding it from the Bukkit shadow jar
- add null guards around login-time player and channel lookups so PacketEvents timing issues do not cascade into Grim exceptions

## Why
Servers that already install the standalone PacketEvents plugin currently end up with two independent PacketEvents injectors when using the Bukkit release jar. This can break login on translated connections and produce duplicate pipeline handling.

By making the Bukkit artifact consistently use the external PacketEvents plugin, one official jar can support PacketEvents-based server setups without shipping a second embedded injector.

## Test plan
- [x] Run `./gradlew :bukkit:shadowJar`
- [x] Verify the generated Bukkit `plugin.yml` contains `depend: [packetevents]`
- [x] Verify the generated Bukkit jar no longer contains bundled PacketEvents classes
- [ ] Reproduce on a Purpur 1.20.1 server with Grim, PacketEvents, and ViaVersion installed

title: feat: Fabric 26.1 official namespace support
body:
## Summary

This PR finalizes Fabric 26.1 official-namespace support and aligns the branch with the validated fork state, including reproducible dependency pinning and multi-platform startup harness coverage.

In addition to the core 26.1 migration updates, this includes end-to-end Grim + PacketEvents harness scripts for Fabric and Bukkit startup validation, plus reproducible setup/run documentation.

## Alignment with architecture guidance

1. **Defaults remain stable**
- Default builds do not depend on local-only artifact behavior.
- Local overrides remain opt-in via `-PmavenLocalOverride=true` / `MAVEN_LOCAL_OVERRIDE=true`.

2. **Reproducible dependency coordinates**
- PacketEvents is pinned to an exact snapshot git coordinate.
- cloud-fabric is pinned to an exact unique snapshot coordinate (no floating `-SNAPSHOT`).

3. **Deterministic resolution behavior**
- Repository strategy and docs are aligned to reproducible defaults with explicit local-override workflows.

## What was added/updated

- Added and hardened Grim + PacketEvents harness scripts under `tests/scripts` for:
  - Fabric official 26.1 bootstrap/startup flow
  - Bukkit Paper 1.20.6 startup flow
  - Bukkit Spigot 1.21.1 startup flow
  - Full-stack runner for combined coverage
- Improved harness reliability:
  - Correct PacketEvents main-jar selection
  - Deterministic timeout/log capture handling
  - Optional `SKIP_CLEAN=true` for faster local iteration without changing CI-safe defaults
- Applied safe cleanup/follow-up fixes in Fabric adapters and docs.

## Proof of tested compatibility

- **Fabric 26.1 (official namespace):** startup harness run with Java 25, successful `Done (...)` marker observed, Grim and PacketEvents initialized.
- **Bukkit Paper 1.20.6:** startup validation completed with successful `Done (...)` marker.
- **Bukkit Spigot 1.21.1:** startup validation completed with successful `Done (...)` marker.

This keeps the older Bukkit startup compatibility path intact while enabling Fabric 26.1 official namespace support.

## Reproduction

### 1) Fabric 26.1 official namespace
- `./tests/scripts/bootstrap-grim-pe-official-261.sh`
- `./tests/scripts/run-server.sh --server-dir tests/runs/grim-pe-26.1 --java-bin /path/to/java25`

### 2) Bukkit Paper 1.20.6
- `./tests/scripts/bootstrap-grim-pe-bukkit-paper-1206.sh`
- `./tests/scripts/run-bukkit-server.sh --server-dir tests/runs/grim-pe-paper-1.20.6`

### 3) Bukkit Spigot 1.21.1
- `./tests/scripts/bootstrap-grim-pe-bukkit-spigot-1211.sh`
- `./tests/scripts/run-bukkit-server.sh --server-dir tests/runs/grim-pe-spigot-1.21.1`

### 4) One-command harness runs
- `./tests/scripts/run-all-grim-pe-harnesses.sh`
- `./tests/scripts/run-all-grim-pe-bukkit-harnesses.sh`
- `./tests/scripts/run-all-grim-pe-stack-harnesses.sh`

## Validation status

- `./gradlew :fabric:compileJava` passes on this branch.
- Harness scripts pass shell syntax checks.
- Startup coverage includes Fabric 26.1 official path, Paper 1.20.6, and Spigot 1.21.1.

---

*Footnote: This PR restores the previously closed PR thread by re-opening from the finalized tip commit (`15f87bd`).*

title: Fix: usingProxy always being false due to error in helper within ProxyAlertMessenger
body:
Fixes #2481

getBooleanFromFile was using Configuralize's DynamicConfig to read external YAML files. DynamicConfig is designed for reading a plugin's own bundled classpath resources, so it was never actually reading the files from disk, causing the method to always return false.

Replaced with SnakeYAML, and manual keying to get the value of the boolean.

Note: DynamicConfig's getBoolean method also accepts {"1", "yes", "on"} as well as "true", while this fix does NOT accept those values.

title: Fix Soul Speed + Swift Sneak simulation false positive on 1.21+
body:
## Description

Fixes continuous simulation false positives when a player with **Swift Sneak 3 leggings** and **Soul Speed 3 boots** is sneaking and bridging over soul sand/soul soil on 1.21+ servers.

## Root Cause

In vanilla 1.21+, Soul Speed is a location_changed enchantment effect ([soul_speed.json](https://github.com/misode/mcmeta/blob/data/data/minecraft/enchantment/soul_speed.json)). When the player steps on a soul speed block, the client applies the movement_efficiency = 1.0 modifier **locally and immediately**. However, the server sends the UPDATE_ATTRIBUTES packet asynchronously.

GrimAC's getBlockSpeedFactor for 1.21+ clients deferred to the MOVEMENT_EFFICIENCY attribute (via getModernVelocityMultiplier), relying on the server-sent value. During bridging where block position changes constantly the attribute updates lagged behind the client's local state, causing GrimAC to predict with movement_efficiency = 0 (soul sand slowdown) while the client used 1.0 (no slowdown).

## Fix

Removed the V_1_21 version gate in getBlockSpeedFactor so Soul Speed is checked directly from the player's boots inventory for **all 1.16.2+ clients**, matching the client's local behavior and avoiding the attribute timing desync.

## Testing

- Player with Swift Sneak 3 + Soul Speed 3, sneaking and bridging over soul sand no longer flags simulation.

title: events: migrate internal firings to GrimAPI 1.3 channel API
body:
Stacks on top of #2600. Consumes GrimAnticheat/GrimAPI#21 — the new
channel-based event dispatch in GrimAPI 1.3.0.0. Every
`eventBus.post(new FooEvent(...))` call-site in the anticheat moves
over to `bus.get(FooEvent.class).fire(...)` with the channel cached on
the carrier, dropping the per-fire event allocation on nine hot paths.

### Changes

- Bump `grim-api` 1.2.5.0 → 1.3.0.0 in `libs.versions.toml`.
- `GrimPlayer` holds a single `public final FlagEvent.Channel flagChannel`
  field, resolved once in the constructor. `Check.flag()` reads it via
  `player.flagChannel.fire(player, this, verbose)` — two getfields, no
  method call, no volatile, no null check.
- Cold paths (`GrimExternalAPI` reload, `PlayerDataManager` join/quit)
  resolve the channel inline — called rarely, not worth the field.
- Hot carriers cache their channel in a final instance field:
  - `OffsetHandler` — CompletePredictionEvent
  - `PacketPingListener` — GrimTransactionSend / GrimTransactionReceived
  - `SetbackTeleportUtil` — GrimTeleportEvent
  - `PunishmentManager` — CommandExecuteEvent
- `GrimACBukkitLoaderPlugin.registerAPIService` — the six Bukkit-bridge
  subscribes (Join/Quit/Reload/Flag/CommandExecute/CompletePrediction)
  switch to `bus.get(E.class).onX(grim, handler)` bound to
  `GrimAPI.INSTANCE.getGrimPlugin()`. Legacy
  `ac.grim.grimac.api.events.*` Bukkit Events are still dispatched via
  `Bukkit.getPluginManager().callEvent(...)`, so downstream plugins
  that listen on those Bukkit events see no change.

### What plugin authors see

`bus.subscribe(ctx, FlagEvent.class, listener)` and `@GrimEventHandler`
still work — both route through each channel's legacy slot and get a
per-thread-pooled event instance.

Plugins wanting zero-alloc typed dispatch:

```java
GrimPlugin grim = api.getGrimPlugin(this);
bus.get(FlagEvent.class).onFlag(grim, (user, check, verbose, cancelled) -> {
    // ...
    return cancelled;
});
```

Or abstract-level (fires for every check subtype, including addon checks):

```java
GrimCheckEvent.Channel abs = (GrimCheckEvent.Channel) bus.get(GrimCheckEvent.class);
abs.onCheck(grim, (user, check, cancelled) -> cancelled);
```

### Priority direction flipped (heads up)

Per the API PR: lower number fires first, higher gets final say. Pre-1.3
Grim sorted highest-first. Plugins using the default priority (0) don't
notice; anyone passing explicit priority numbers on `@GrimEventHandler`
or `bus.subscribe(...)` will want to re-evaluate their numbers.

### Testing

- `./gradlew build` passes across common / bukkit / fabric.
- Against paper-1.21.11 with a reference plugin wired to every channel
  plus abstract `GrimCheckEvent` + `GrimEvent` subscribes:
  - Join / Quit / Reload / TxSend / TxRecv fire end-to-end through the
    new `bus.get(E.class).onX(grim, handler)` path
  - Legacy `@GrimEventHandler` still dispatches when plugins use it
  - `GrimEvent.onAnyEvent` fires on Join via the bridge in each concrete
    channel
- Wurst Flight against paper-1.21.11:
  - Typed FlagEvent handler fires on the netty thread
  - Abstract `GrimCheckEvent.onCheck` bridge fires at the same time,
    receiving the shared (user, check, cancelled) destructure

title: Feat: Add toggle for Polymer block translation hook
body:
This simply adds a toggle for Grim's polymer hook.

Why?
It makes it so ViaFabric, ViaBackwards, Grim, and Polymer all play nice together. The issue is that Polymer allows you to disable its networking in its own config, but Grim doesn't have a way to 'see' that change. If Polymer's networking is off but Grim keeps trying to hook into it, it causes some weird packet junk I don't understand at all. This setting lets you manually tell Grim to stop hooking into Polymer, making it way easier to keep all four mods so you don't have to recompile Grim just for this niche bug.

title: datastore: history rewrite: five backends, session-based, ring-buffer write path + universal config autoupdater
body:
History rewrite. \`/grim history\` switches from "every flag in chronological order" to **session-based** — joining the server starts a session row, leaving (or crashing) closes it, every flag during that session is keyed to it via the session's UUID. Sessions are the natural unit for retention rules, the natural unit for paginating, and they let the per-flag insert path defer to a Disruptor ring instead of doing JDBC on the netty thread.

**Routing & backends.** New \`database.yml\` (master toggle + per-category routing) plus a per-backend file under \`databases/<id>/\`. Each DataStore category — violation / session / player-identity / setting / blob — routes to a backend independently, so you can mix (SQLite for sessions, Mongo for blobs, etc.). Five \`BackendProvider\`s ship: SQLite, MySQL, Postgres, Mongo, Redis. Drivers come in via the platform library loader as **separate Modrinth holder mods/plugins**, not bundled into Grim — keeps the jar small and lets people opt into networked DBs without a JDBC dep on every install. Missing driver → backend self-disables on startup with a clear log line, routing falls over to whatever else is configured, server still starts.

**Write path.** \`recordFlagFromCheck\` (called from \`[log]\` in PunishmentManager) publishes onto a Disruptor ring; the producer fills a preallocated event slot and returns. On a full ring the record is dropped and counted in \`DataStore.metrics()\` — producers never block. The old \`ViolationDatabaseManager\` is gone. Default \`[log]\` cadence in \`punishments.yml\` dropped from \`5:5\` etc. to \`1:1\` since the ring keeps up.

**Lifecycle & crash recovery.** Sessions open from \`PlayerDataManager.onDisconnect\`, kept current by a 30s heartbeat in \`pollData\` upserting \`last_activity_epoch_ms\`. Server crash with players online → next boot's sweep stamps \`closed_at = last_activity\` on every still-open row via the new \`markCrashedSessions()\` SPI on each backend, and those sessions render with a \`(crashed)\` marker.

**Config updater.** Cross-version, runs before load. Bumped \`config-version\` and added \`config-flavor\` (V2/V3) schema markers on every yml. \`config.yml\` v9 → v10 migration lifts the old inline \`history:\` block into \`database.yml\` plus the matching per-backend file via cross-file writes. Backups go to \`<file>.v<N>.bak\` per migration. \`punishments.yml\` is intentionally exempt — it's operator-authored.

**\`/grim history\` shapes.**
- \`/grim history <player>\` — session list, newest first
- \`/grim history <player> page <N>\` — jump to page N of the session list
- \`/grim history <player> session <N|latest> [-d] [-v]\` — session detail (most recent violations first)
- \`/grim history <player> session <N|latest> page <N> [-d] [-v]\` — session detail, violation page N
- \`-d\` switches from grouped-by-check rollup to one line per violation; \`-v\` adds verbose debug output

**API surface** (\`@ApiStatus.Experimental\`):
- \`HistoryService\` — paged session list, single-session detail, total session count. The same surface \`/grim history\` reads from, so any third-party UI (web dashboard, alt command framework, RCON tooling) gets the same data without reimplementing.
- \`DataStore\` — submit / query / delete + \`forgetPlayer(uuid)\` for GDPR-style wipes + \`metrics()\` for queue-depth and drop counters.

**Other.**
- V0 → V1 migration on first boot if \`data/violations.sqlite\` is present. Legacy file left intact as a safety net — the new store writes into a fresh \`data/history.v1.db\` and never \`ALTER\`s the old one. Also exposed as \`/grim history migrate [--delete]\` for manual runs.
- \`/grim alerts|brands|verbose\` toggles persist across leave/join via the \`setting\` category.
- 92 yml files across 10+ locales got the V2 history strings + per-backend translations.

### Things to keep in mind for future work

- The \`[log]\` write path is fire-and-forget through the ring. Failures count into \`metrics()\` but don't propagate to the alert path. If a future alert mode needs durable confirmation, go through \`DataStore.query\` / a direct backend write — not the ring.
- \`CheckRegistry.intern(...)\` is \`synchronized\`. Cold path in practice (per-checkname, cached in \`LiveWriteHooksImpl.checkIdCache\` after first hit), but if it ever moves to a hot path, see the TODO on \`intern\` for what a lock-free rewrite would need.
- \`closed_at\` carries a "once-set" invariant on every backend — every writer \`COALESCE\`/\`\$ifNull\`s on it. Don't overwrite without a migration plan.
- Configuralize uses all-or-nothing per-locale fallback. New message keys must land in every bundled non-en yml at the same time, otherwise non-en users see a missing-key error rather than falling through to en.yml.
- Schema markers (\`config-flavor\` / \`config-version\`) on every operator-facing yml. The updater rejects a wrong-flavor file (e.g. V3 config opened by V2 jar) instead of silently flat-merging into the wrong key set. New yml files in the GrimAC data folder need both markers.

### Tested on

Paper 1.21.11 against the per-zone test-data containers (Mongo 8, Postgres 16, MySQL 8.4, Redis 8) plus SQLite. V0 → V1 migration verified against a populated legacy \`violations.sqlite\`. Cross-version updater verified config v9 (Grim 2.x) → v10. Lower MC versions (1.8.8 → 1.20.4) covered against the SQLite path with the sqlite-jdbc holder mod.

title: CraftEngine custom block support
body:
CraftEngine register custom blocks into PacketEvents as custom StateTypes (e.g. craftengine:custom_0). These blocks are rendered client-side using vanilla block shapes (fences, slabs, stairs, trapdoors, etc.).

### Problem
Grim collision system in `CollisionData#getData()` does not recognize custom StateTypes. Because of this, unknown blocks always fall back to `DEFAULT`, which is a full 1x1x1 cube:

https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/blob/2.0/common/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/utils/collisions/CollisionData.java#L1174-L1181

As a result, Grim simulates all CraftEngine custom blocks as full blocks, regardless of their actual vanilla-based shape

### Impact
This causes incorrect anti-cheat flags:

- **Simulation false positives**
  - when colliding with non-full blocks (fences, walls, stairs, etc.)
- **GroundSpoof flags**
  - when standing on non-full blocks (slabs, trapdoors, etc.)

Full-cube custom blocks (e.g. stone, planks) are unaffected, since they match `DEFAULT`

### Important notes
- `disable-default-resync-handler` does not help
- The issue is not syncing or desync-related
- It is strictly collision simulation using incorrect fallback data

### Reproduction
1. Install CraftEngine with `inject-packetevents: true`
2. Place a custom block based on a non-full vanilla block (fence, slab, stairs, etc)
3. Walk into or stand on it
4. Run `/grim verbose`

Result: Simulation / GroundSpoof flags are triggered

### Current limitation
There is currently no way for plugins to register custom collision mappings for custom StateTypes. Because of this, CraftEngine blocks cannot provide correct collision data to Grim

### Suggested improvement
A possible solution would be to add an extension point for custom collision resolution, e.g.:

- StateType -> CollisionData provider hook
- or external collision override registry

This would allow plugins like CraftEngine to map custom blocks back to their correct vanilla collision shapes

title: Mid-Air Freeze
body:
### Describe the bypass and how to replicate it

There is a bypass where a player can remain permanently suspended in mid-air without triggering a setback or kick from Grim. When a player uses this method, Grim fails to set the player back to a valid location, allowing them to remain frozen in the air for an extended period without being forced to fall.

### Impact/Abuse:
Players can delay death from falling. Additionally, because they are positioned in mid-air, they gain a positional advantage that allows them to remain out of reach and safe from attacks by other players and entities. In this state, players can break blocks and use commands.

### Replicate:
Mod link: https://modrinth.com/mod/freecam/versions
Video: https://youtu.be/lEOYLJkH44A
1. Enable the "Freeze Player" option within the Freecam settings.
2. Jump or fall so that your character is in mid-air.
3. Activate a "Freecam" mod.
4. The player character will now be completely frozen in mid-air.

title: Fix book page length check
body:
The book page length was limited to 256 characters. This limit was the hard character length limit in versions 1.13 and below, but it was increased to 1023 in 1.14 and above. This PR simply adds adds an additional check of the client version to limit the page length correctly.

This issue was regularly encountered by players writing books normally on my server, indicating that it is easy for modern clients to reach the 256 character limit.

title: GrimAC 2.3.73 incompatibility with PacketEvents 2.12.1 causing all interaction packets to disconnect players on Purpur 1.21.11
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

Environment:

* Purpur: 1.21.11 build 2566
* GrimAC: 2.3.73
* PacketEvents: 2.12.1
* Latest Geyser + Floodgate
* ViaVersion installed
* Java 21

Issue:
Players can join and move normally, but as soon as they interact with anything (inventory clicks, opening containers, item interactions, etc.) they are disconnected with "Invalid packet".

This affects BOTH:

* Java players
* Bedrock players through Geyser

The issue disappears immediately after removing GrimAC.

Important detail:
Another plugin (CustomDiscs) requires PacketEvents and auto-installs the standalone PacketEvents plugin. Removing PacketEvents causes CustomDiscs to fail loading.

Error:

```text
Failed to map the Packet ID 67 to a PacketType constant.
Bound: SERVER, Connection state: PLAY, Server version: 1.21.11

* Movement packets work normally
* Interaction packets immediately disconnect players
* Removing Grim fixes the problem completely
* Updating Geyser and standalone PacketEvents did not fix the issue

packet sequence probably looks something like this in the last breaking tick:
movement -> destroy -> arm animation -> client_tick_end

title: punishment: anchor N:M intervals at N
body:
Grim's `punishments.yml` has not done what its documentation claims for a while. It does not fire for the first time at N at intervals of M. It can be off by 1 on first group flag and the interval calculation requires N be a multiple of itself after second punishment trigger.

The full technical explanation: 
`shouldExecute` did `violationCount % command.interval == 0`, which anchors fires to multiples of M regardless of where N sits. The default Simulation group has `100:40 [alert]` and the en.yml comment claims `100:50` fires "every 50th flag after 100" where neither matches `vc % M`. `100:40` fires on flag 121/161/201 today (the surrounding off-by-one `>= threshold` gate also pushes it one further); should be 100/140/180.

Switch the inline expression to `(violationCount - command.threshold) % command.interval == 0` so the schedule is N, N+M, N+2M, ... like the comment promises. Also updated `punishments/en.yml` to describe the schedule honestly with examples for both aligned and non-aligned configs.

Configs (`100:50`, `100:100`, `25:25`, `5:5`) are unchanged, this is technically a behavior change but it does the expected behaviour.

title: [Bug] NPE in BukkitPlatformPlayer on PlayerJoin when channel is null (reconnect during protocol change)
body:
## Description

GrimAC throws `NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "io.netty.channel.Channel.pipeline()" because "channel" is null` during the `UserLoginEvent` / `PlayerJoinEvent` when a player reconnects immediately after a connection was closed during a protocol change. GrimAC tries to build a `BukkitPlatformPlayer` which fetches the channel pipeline via `ProtocolManager.getUser()`, but the channel object is `null` because the previous connection was already torn down.

## Server Information

```
GrimAC: 2.3.74-a3a95cc
Server: CanvasMC 26.1.2 (Folia fork, build 748-31c2d7f)
packetevents (shaded): bundled with GrimAC
Java: OpenJDK 21
```

## Full Stack Trace

```
[21:55:07] [Folia Region Scheduler Thread #2/INFO]: Connection closed during protocol change
[21:55:07] [Folia Region Scheduler Thread #2/WARN]: [ac.grim.grimac.shaded.com.github.retrooper.packetevents.PacketEventsAPI] PacketEvents caught an unhandled exception while calling your listener.
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "io.netty.channel.Channel.pipeline()" because "channel" is null
	at grimac-bukkit-2.3.74-a3a95cc.jar//ac.grim.grimac.shaded.io.github.retrooper.packetevents.netty.channel.ChannelOperatorModernImpl.getPipeline(ChannelOperatorModernImpl.java:85)
	at grimac-bukkit-2.3.74-a3a95cc.jar//ac.grim.grimac.shaded.com.github.retrooper.packetevents.netty.channel.ChannelHelper.getPipeline(ChannelHelper.java:85)

	at grimac-bukkit-2.3.74-a3a95cc.jar//ac.grim.grimac.platform.bukkit.player.BukkitPlatformPlayerFactory.createPlatformPlayer(BukkitPlatformPlayerFactory.java:30)
	at grimac-bukkit-2.3.74-a3a95cc.jar//ac.grim.grimac.platform.bukkit.player.BukkitPlatformPlayerFactory.createPlatformPlayer(BukkitPlatformPlayerFactory.java:16)
	at grimac-bukkit-2.3.74-a3a95cc.jar//ac.grim.grimac.platform.api.player.AbstractPlatformPlayerFactory.getFromNativePlayerType(AbstractPlatformPlayerFactory.java:59)
	at grimac-bukkit-2.3.74-a3a95cc.jar//ac.grim.grimac.events.packets.PacketPlayerJoinQuit.onUserLogin(PacketPlayerJoinQuit.java:40)
	at grimac-bukkit-2.3.74-a3a95cc.jar//ac.grim.grimac.shaded.com.github.retrooper.packetevents.event.UserLoginEvent.call(UserLoginEvent.java:47)
	at grimac-bukkit-2.3.74-a3a95cc.jar//ac.grim.grimac.shaded.com.github.retrooper.packetevents.event.EventManager.callEvent(EventManager.java:85)
	at grimac-bukkit-2.3.74-a3a95cc.jar//ac.grim.grimac.shaded.com.github.retrooper.packetevents.event.EventManager.callEvent(EventManager.java:103)
	at grimac-bukkit-2.3.74-a3a95cc.jar//ac.grim.grimac.shaded.com.github.retrooper.packetevents.event.EventManager.callEvent(EventManager.java:67)
	at grimac-bukkit-2.3.74-a3a95cc.jar//ac.grim.grimac.shaded.io.github.retrooper.packetevents.bukkit.InternalGlobalBukkitListener.onPlayerJoin(InternalGlobalBukkitListener.java:34)
	at co.aikar.timings.TimedEventExecutor.execute(TimedEventExecutor.java:80)
	at org.bukkit.plugin.RegisteredListener.callEvent(RegisteredListener.java:71)
	at io.papermc.paper.plugin.manager.PaperEventManager.callEvent(PaperEventManager.java:57)
	at net.minecraft.server.players.PlayerList.placeNewPlayer(PlayerList.java:316)
	at net.minecraft.server.network.config.PrepareSpawnTask$Ready.spawn(PrepareSpawnTask.java:393)
	at net.minecraft.server.network.config.PrepareSpawnTask.spawnPlayer(PrepareSpawnTask.java:168)
	at net.minecraft.server.network.ServerConfigurationPacketListenerImpl.lambda$handleConfigurationFinished$2(ServerConfigurationPacketListenerImpl.java:257)
	at io.papermc.paper.threadedregions.RegionizedTaskQueue$PrioritisedQueue$ChunkBasedPriorityTask.executeInternal(RegionizedTaskQueue.java:545)
	at io.papermc.paper.threadedregions.RegionizedTaskQueue$RegionTaskQueueData.drainTasks(RegionizedTaskQueue.java:294)
	at net.minecraft.server.dedicated.DedicatedServer.tickServer(DedicatedServer.java:465)
	at io.papermc.paper.threadedregions.TickRegions$ConcreteRegionTickHandle.tickRegion(TickRegions.java:519)
	at io.papermc.paper.threadedregions.TickRegionScheduler$RegionScheduleHandle.runTick(TickRegionScheduler.java:524)
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run GrimAC 2.3.74 on CanvasMC 26.1.2 (Folia-based)
2. Player connects; during login the message `Connection closed during protocol change` is logged
3. The same player reconnects immediately after
4. GrimAC fires `UserLoginEvent` / `onPlayerJoin` for the new connection
5. NPE thrown in `BukkitPlatformPlayer.<init>` because `channel` is null

## Expected Behavior

GrimAC handles the case where the player's channel is null (stale previous connection) gracefully — either by skipping initialization for that join event, or by null-checking the channel before calling `channel.pipeline()`.

## Root Cause

`ProtocolManager.getUser()` at line 151 calls `ChannelHelper.getPipeline()` → `ChannelOperatorModernImpl.getPipeline()` → `channel.pipeline()`. When a connection is closed during a protocol change and the player immediately reconnects, the channel object associated with the old connection may still be referenced as `null`. A null check for the channel before calling `.pipeline()` would prevent the crash.

title: [Bug] PacketProcessException: Failed to map Packet ID 31 in CONFIGURATION state for 1.16.4 clients (via ViaVersion)
body:
## Version

**GrimAC 2.3.74-e32d091**

## Environment

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Server software** | CanvasMC 26.1.2 (Folia fork, build 752-85cc447) |
| **Minecraft version** | 1.21.x |
| **ViaVersion** | present (`preVia: true` in error context) |
| **Client version** | 1.16.4 |
| **Java** | OpenJDK 21 |

## Bug Description

When a player connects with a 1.16.4 client (translated by ViaVersion), GrimAC's shaded PacketEvents throws `PacketProcessException: Failed to map the Packet ID 31 to a PacketType constant` during the `CONFIGURATION` connection phase. The error fires 3 times per connection attempt (once per reconnect cycle observed), logged as WARN on the Netty IO thread.

This is a **separate issue** from #2662 (NPE on channel null). The NPE is on join; this error is during the protocol negotiation/configuration phase before the player is fully joined. The client does eventually connect despite the warnings, but the spam may mask real errors.

body:
Server can send a SET_PLAYER_INVENTORY packet with a slot ID that equals or exceeds the tracked slot count (e.g. slot 46 on a 46-slot player inventory), causing an uncaught IndexOutOfBoundsException in the latency transaction lambda. Added a bounds check to skip the update silently when the slot ID is out of range.

Reproduced with Asteroid fake players on Leaf 1.21.11.

title: command/history: V2 backport — session help, player escape, prefix-on-header, sanitisation
body:
Three operator-facing changes to `/grim history`:

- `/grim history <target> session` (no ordinal) prints the help menu instead of Cloud's stock `missing required argument: session` parse error.
- `/grim history player <target> …` disambiguates player names that collide with a sibling literal at the same tree depth (today: `repair`, `player` itself).
- Fallback history templates render `%prefix%` on header lines only; mid-render rows render unprefixed. Operators' existing `messages.yml` overrides are unaffected — only the hard-coded defaults change.

## How it works

`HistoryComponentRenderer.mmSafe()` is the sanitization layer for untrusted leaves — client brand, inline verbose text, player display, check display/description. Strips `%` before legacy `§`/`&` markers (so `&%c` cannot become `&c` after the percent drops out), strips hex variants (`&#RRGGBB` and the Bedrock `&x&R&R…` interleave), and escapes the MiniMessage tag opener. The legacy regex is narrowed to the canonical Minecraft alphabet (`0-9 a-f k-o r x`) so innocent text like `R&D` or `AT&T` survives untouched.

Server name, Grim version, the renderer-built `crashed_marker` and `checks_list`, and templates loaded from `messages.yml` pass through verbatim so operator-authored formatting still works.

## What this prevents

- A crafted client brand or check name painting MiniMessage into operator-facing rows.
- A leaf value expanding `%prefix%` / `%grim_version%` to lift trusted text through the downstream placeholder replacer.
- A `<click:run_command:/op …>` slipping past the renderer via any untrusted field.

## Test plan

- [ ] `/grim history <target> session` prints the session help menu.
- [ ] `/grim history player <colliding-name>` resolves a player named e.g. `repair`.
- [ ] Bare forms still work for list, paged list, session detail, paged session detail.
- [ ] Fallback history output only carries the bot prefix on header lines; existing `messages.yml` overrides remain unchanged.
- [ ] Untrusted client brand (e.g. `§cVape` or `<click:run_command:/op …>vape</click>`) renders as plain text in `/grim history` output.

title: Fabric PlatformPlayer location can stay stale after respawn or dimension change
body:
## Describe the bug and how to replicate it
On Fabric, cached PlatformPlayer instances update their `fabricPlayer` reference in `replaceNativePlayer(...)` when Minecraft replaces the `ServerPlayer` during respawn or dimension-change handling. However, the superclass `AbstractFabricGrimEntity` keeps its original native `entity` reference. Inherited methods such as `getLocation()`, `getWorld()`, `distanceSquared(...)`, and `eject()` can therefore continue reading the stale entity.

This can make `/grim spectate <target>` teleport to the target's old location after the target respawns or changes dimensions, because `GrimSpectate` reads `targetPlatformPlayer.getLocation()`.

Minimal replication:

1. Run a Fabric server with Grim and Fabric API.
2. Join with a spectator account and a target player.
3. Ensure the target's PlatformPlayer has been cached by Grim.
4. Have the target die and respawn, or change dimensions so Minecraft replaces the `ServerPlayer`.
5. Run `/grim spectate <target>`.
6. Observe that the spectate teleport can use the target's stale pre respawn or pre dimension change location instead of the current player location.

Expected: cached PlatformPlayer location/world reads use the current native `ServerPlayer`.

Actual: inherited entity-backed location/world reads can remain tied to the old native entity.

Suggested fix: when Fabric `replaceNativePlayer(...)` runs, also refresh the entity reference used by `AbstractFabricGrimEntity`.

## Grim version
Observed on `2.3.74-0b7001b`.

Also present in current upstream `2.0` source as of commit `490a02b7b`.

## Server version
Fabric server on Minecraft 1.21.11.

## Affected Platform(s)
Fabric

## Plugins/Mods
- Fabric API
- Grim

title: fix(fabric): refresh wrapped player entity on respawn
body:
## Summary
- Keep Fabric GrimEntity's native entity reference in sync when a cached PlatformPlayer is rebound after Minecraft replaces the ServerPlayer.
- Prevent inherited PlatformPlayer location/world/distance reads from using the old pre-respawn or pre-dimension-change entity.
- Fix Fabric `/grim spectate <player>` teleporting to stale target coordinates after the target respawns or changes dimensions.

## Notes
- This is Fabric-only. Bukkit wrappers do not use this Fabric entity/player split.
- Fixes https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/issues/2691.

## Testing
- `./gradlew :fabric:compileJava :fabric:mc12111:compileJava`

title: Simulation false positive on Fabric 1.21.11 after 2.3.74-36931a8
body:
## Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

A `Simulation` false positive is reproducible on a clean Fabric 1.21.11 test backend running only GrimAC, Fabric API, and Fabric Bungee Forwarding shortly after exiting a portal.

This appears to have started with `2.3.74-36931a8` (`migrate more checks to pre-via`). The same test did not reproduce on the earlier known-good build `2.3.74-0b7001b`, but still reproduces on latest `2.3.74-490a02b`.

Reproduction setup:

1. Start a Fabric 1.21.11 backend with only:
   - GrimAC
   - Fabric API
   - Fabric Bungee Forwarding
2. Join with a vanilla 1.21.11 client.
3. Enter a portal
4. Grim repeatedly flags `Simulation` for a few seconds.

Expected behavior: vanilla movement should not flag `Simulation` in this minimal setup.

## Grim Log

https://paste.grim.ac/02AM6cyUuz

## Grim version

Latest tested, still reproduces:
`2.3.74-490a02b`

First bad build identified:
`2.3.74-36931a8`

Known-good build:
`2.3.74-0b7001b`

## Server version

Fabric server on Minecraft `1.21.11`.

## Client version

Vanilla `1.21.11`

## Plugins/Mods

Backend mods:

- GrimAC `2.3.74-490a02b`
- Fabric API `0.141.4+1.21.11`
- Fabric Bungee Forwarding `0.1.16+1.21.11`

Proxy:

- Velocity with player forwarding enabled

title: Fabric: support Minecraft 26.X on official mappings
body:
Adds Grim Fabric support for Minecraft 26.X on official (Mojang) mappings while keeping 1.16.1-1.21.11 intermediary support in the same published jar.

## Structure
The jar now nests three Fabric variants:
- fabric-common contains shared platform code with no Minecraft classpath and ships unremapped.
- fabric-intermediary is remapped to intermediary and runs on 1.16.1-1.21.11.
- fabric-official compiles against the deobfuscated 26.X jar and runs on 26.1.x, with mc261 submodules for version-specific entrypoints.

Each nested variant declares its depends.minecraft range, so Fabric activates one variant for the server version. Shared platform code reaches Minecraft classes through injected platform handles (FabricServerPlayerHandle, FabricMinecraftServerHandle, FabricEntityHandle) added with Loom injected-interfaces and Mixin `@Implements`. The common code owns the logic, and each mapping supplies the method bodies.

## Dependency
Depends on the paired PacketEvents PR (GrimAnticheat/packetevents#13), pinned as 2.12.2+0db7c6971. That PacketEvents build needs to be published before this builds for other developers.

## Testing
Tested both runtimes:
- 1.21.11 intermediary: clean boot, player join, hacks flag.
- 26.1.2 official: clean boot; a 1.21.11 client joined through ViaVersion and stayed connected; Wurst Flight flagged Simulation, GroundSpoof, and AntiKB with setback.

Also checked fabric-common bytecode for net.minecraft references; any reference there would ship unremapped and break intermediary.


Closes https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/pull/2692 https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/issues/2691 https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/issues/2554 https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/issues/2551

title: Players get kicked with "Disconnected" and no console errors
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

Players are being kicked with the disconnect reason: "Disconnected".

There are no related errors or warnings in the console before the kick. The console does not show any useful log explaining the reason.

I tested this on multiple server jars/cores, but the issue still happens.

I also removed all other plugins and tested with only Grim installed, but players still get kicked with the same "Disconnected" reason.

I tested packet-spam-threshold set to 1000 in the Grim config. The default value is 100, so it does not seem to be caused by that setting.

There are no obvious errors before the kick, only a normal disconnect message.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Start the server with Grim installed.
2. Join the server.
3. Play for a while.
4. The player gets kicked with the reason "Disconnected".
5. No useful error appears in the console before the kick.

title: fix(fabric): bind PacketContext around item encoding for Polymer 0.16+ (#2701)
body:
## Fixes #2701 — Fabric 26.x + Polymer item-encode crash

### Symptom
On Fabric MC 26.x with Polymer installed, holding/receiving any item spams:
```
Failed to encode ItemStack: {}64 minecraft:stripped_oak_log: java.lang.RuntimeException: PacketContext is required, but it wasn't set up!
    at net.fabricmc.fabric.api.networking.v1.context.PacketContext.orElseThrow(PacketContext.java:148)
```
Every affected read returns `ItemStack.EMPTY`, so Grim sees players holding nothing.

### Root cause
Grim encodes `ItemStack`s outside the Netty pipeline when reading a player's inventory (`fromFabricItemStack` → `ItemStack.STREAM_CODEC.encode`). Polymer 0.16+ (26.x) mixes into that codec and calls fabric-api `PacketContext.orElseThrow()` for **every** item, which throws when no context is bound to the thread. Polymer ≤1.21.x used PacketTweaker, which tolerated a missing context — so the item path was never protected; the 26.x switch to fabric-api's strict context surfaced it. (Prior Polymer work only covered block translation.)

### Fix
- `FabricItemContextHook` (new, `fabric/shared`): reflectively binds the inventory owner's `PacketContext` via `PacketContext.supplyWithContext(provider, supplier)` around the encode. Gated by a `static final ACTIVE` flag (JIT-folds to a no-op when Polymer / the fabric-api context API is absent, so non-Polymer servers and the intermediary/≤1.21.11 variant keep the original allocation-free path). Uses `invokeExact`.
- `AbstractFabricPlatformInventory`: routes reads through the gate (one bind per `getContents` sweep).
- `Fabric261ConversionUtil`: fix a malformed `"…: {}" + stack` log line.

### Verification (live, `fabric-26.1.2` + Polymer 0.16.5)
- Pre-fix: **32** `PacketContext is required` errors (incl. exact `{}64 minecraft:stripped_oak_log`).
- This PR: **0** errors; instrumented the bind path and observed `bind SUCCESS via net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer` (fabric-api's `ServerPlayerMixin` makes `ServerPlayer` a `PacketContextProvider`). No regressions; both variants compile.

title: exempt Bedrock players by username dot-prefix + %grim_isbedrock…
body:
…% placeholder

Geyser/Floodgate prefix Bedrock usernames with "." by default. Treat a leading-dot username as a Bedrock player and exempt them from checks, in addition to the existing Geyser/Floodgate API and Geyser-UUID detection. This covers setups where the Geyser/Floodgate API isn't reachable from the anticheat (e.g. proxy installs).

Adds GeyserUtil.isBedrockName() as the shared dot-prefix check used by both the exemption path and the new %grim_isbedrock% PlaceholderAPI placeholder. The placeholder resolves directly from the username so it still returns true for Bedrock players, who are exempted and therefore have no tracked GrimPlayer.

## Summary
- Use the released GrimAPI 1.6.0.1 storage fixes.
- Keep datastore startup route-aware so one failed backend disables only the affected datastore features.
- Resolve no-op datastore facades at startup/reload instead of branching in hot paths.
- Preserve optional SQLite JDBC driver-holder behavior; Fabric does not shade SQLite.

Fixes #2707
Fixes #2710

title: Players with flight enabled bypass speed checks (unbounded fly speed causes server lag)
body:
### Describe the bypass and how to replicate it

### Description

When a player has flight enabled (`Player#setAllowFlight(true)` / `setFlying(true)`),
Grim currently skips movement/speed checks for them. As a result these players can
move far faster than the server-side allowed flight speed without being flagged,
which makes fly-speed cheats undetectable for any player who has flight permission.

The speed is effectively unbounded — a cheating player can fly 10x (or more) the
normal speed. Besides being unfair, this causes serious server-side performance
issues: rapid movement forces excessive chunk loading and entity/movement
processing, leading to noticeable server lag (TPS drops). This makes it a
stability problem, not just a fairness one.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Give a player flight permission (e.g. a `/fly` command or `allow flight`).
2. While flying, use a client/mod that increases flight speed.
3. Observe that Grim does not flag or limit the abnormal flight speed, and that
   very high speeds cause server lag.

### Expected behavior

Grim should still validate flying players' speed against the server-side allowed
flight speed (`AbilitiesPacket` fly speed) and flag/cancel movement that exceeds it,
instead of ignoring flying players entirely.

### Actual behavior

Flying players are effectively exempt from speed enforcement, so fly-speed cheats
go undetected and can reach extreme speeds that degrade server performance.



### Grim version

2.3.74-67aa3a9

### Server version

[Canvas] 26.1.2 | HEAD#796 [b34853b] | STABLE

### Client version

26.1.12

### Plugins/Mods

- FancyHolograms, FancyNpcs, PlugManX

title: Crash Server
body:
### Stack trace

spark https://iimg.su/i/LLQSwc

### How to replicate it if known

I don't know how, but my server only gets taken down if Grimac is running on it.
I’m not a programmer, but the server is definitely being crashed on purpose. I have a lot of players on the server, and they weren't able to crash the game modes where GrimAC was disabled.

Yes, almost exactly.

The player sent a position packet saying: "I'm now at coordinates X/Y/Z." If the distance from the previous position is large, Grim still reaches the part of its logic where it calculates the movement volume for this tick between the old and new positions.

Then Grim performs this check:

Did the player's hitbox intersect a Nether Portal block during this movement tick?

To do this, it doesn't ray trace or just check two points. Instead, it constructs a large bounding box covering the entire path between the old and new positions and calls hasMaterial(), which iterates through the blocks inside that bounding box.

So with a large movement:

small normal movement box
→ becomes a large box
→ Grim scans many blocks
→ the load falls on the Netty thread

The player doesn't actually need to enter a portal. Here, the portal is simply a block material that Grim searches for inside the movement volume.

If the volume is large, the search itself becomes expensive.

An important clarification: Grim is not "fully simulating a teleport over a huge distance" specifically because of the portal. The main prediction logic is also running, but according to the Spark profile, the hottest code path was the updateNetherPortalState() check.
