title: fix usingProxy always returning false (#2481)
body:
usingProxy in ProxyAlertMessenger was unconditionally false regardless of 'spigot.yml'/'paper.ym'/'paper-global.yml' settings, because the config lookup relied on configuralize's DynamicConfig, which requires a bundled classpath "defaults" resource that never existed for this ad-hoc read, every call silently threw and fell back to false.

Replaced the lookup with a direct SnakeYaml read that walks the dotted key path manually, with no dependency on a nonexistent bundled resource

Fixes #2481

title: CompensatedWorld chunks race condition. Setback loop.
body:
### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it

1. Install EssentialsSpawn and create a second world (I'll call it World 2).
2. Set the spawn in World 2 using `/setspawn` (I used coordinates `0 0` on the highest block).
3. Join the server with a completely new account that has never connected before.

What happens is that the player initially joins in the default world, and then EssentialsSpawn immediately teleports them to World 2.

I added debug logging and found that the `PacketType.Play.Server.CHUNK_DATA` packets (handled by `BasePacketWorldReader`) for World 2 arrive before `player.compensatedWorld.chunks.clear()` is called while handling `PacketType.Play.Server.RESPAWN` in `PacketPlayerRespawn`.

Because of this, those chunk entries are cleared after they've already been received, and no replacement chunk packets arrive afterwards. As a result, the checks believe the player is standing in an unloaded chunk, which causes the infinite setback loop.

I looked for a way to force the `CompensatedWorld` to refresh or re-request chunk data, but I couldn't find one. I initially expected the resyncs in `SetbackTeleportUtil` to handle this, but they don't seem to.

For now I've implemented a temporary workaround: if I detect this situation, I cache the affected chunk data and restore it after `player.compensatedWorld.chunks.clear()` is called. It works around the problem, but it definitely feels like a hack. I'm hoping there's a more correct way to solve this, or that it can be fixed in Grim itself.


### Grim Log

.

### Grim version

2.3.74

### Server version

SSSpigot 1.16.5

### Client version

Vanilla 1.21.4

EssentialsSpawn

title: Fix nether portal sweep for teleport-sized movement
body:
Fixed a severe nether portal collision check issue where large server-side teleports could trigger an enormous movement sweep, causing packet-thread stalls and making the server unusable.

`updateNetherPortalState()` expanded the player’s current bounding box using the delta between the previous and current position. This works fine for normal movement, but large teleports or position corrections can make that delta span a huge area. As a result, the portal collision query could scan a very large region during movement packet handling.

On the live Folia server where this was observed, the issue caused all players to time out, spammed the server console with repeated keepalive timeout disconnect logs, and left the server unable to accept new connections or restart cleanly.

The fix keeps the normal per-tick movement sweep for portal detection, but avoids doing oversized portal collision sweeps for teleport-sized or invalid movement deltas.

Added unit coverage for normal, oversized, and non-finite deltas. Also validated with `./gradlew.bat common:check` and tested in-game on the same live Folia server. The same large `/home` teleport no longer reproduces the pathological portal collision scan.

Related to #2767 and #2791

title: Fix Simulation false flags when colliding with sulfur spikes
body:
## What
Apply the 0.125 max horizontal model-offset clamp to `SULFUR_SPIKE` in `OffsetCollisionBox`, the same clamp already used for `POINTED_DRIPSTONE`. Sulfur spikes share dripstone's collision shape via `CollisionData.POINTED_DRIPSTONE`, but fell through to the default 0.25 clamp.

## Why
The client clamps a sulfur spike's random XZ model offset to +/-0.125 (same as pointed dripstone). For any spike whose raw per-position hash offset exceeds 0.125, Grim placed its collision box up to ~0.09 blocks away from where the client has it. Walking into such a spike then false flags Simulation (offsets ~0.01-0.02, repeating while the player is pressed against the spike).

## Verification
Reproduced against a Simulation debug dump (26.2, vanilla client) and checked the math directly:
- Spike at (-2877, -3123): with the 0.125 clamp its -X face sits at exactly x = -2876.8125, matching the client's stuck position; the dump's "Actually" movement of 0.07812360173011257 is exactly the distance to that face. With the 0.25 clamp the box shifts to x = -2876.904, which the player's bounding box already intersected, so the simulation ignored the collision and predicted free movement - producing the flagged offset.
- Spike at (-2877, -3125): with the 0.125 clamp its +Z face is exactly the player's stuck minZ = -3124.4375; with 0.25 it lands at -3124.529 and the collision is missed.

`:bukkit:shadowJar` builds and the packaged `OffsetCollisionBox` class was verified (via javap) to contain the fix.

title: CompensatedWorld.getChunk() / containsNetherPortal() consumes 40-60%+ of Netty IO thread CPU, causing connection timeouts under load
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

Under sustained load, several of our 8 Netty Epoll IO threads become pinned 
at 100% CPU, escalating over time from 3/8 to 6/8 threads maxed. This causes 
players to experience read timeouts / failed connections to the backend 
(via Velocity proxy), since PacketEventsDecoder.decode() runs synchronously 
inside the Netty IO thread and blocks packet processing for all connections 
sharing that thread.

Two spark profiles captured minutes apart during the same incident show the 
same call path scaling proportionally with severity:

--- Profile 1 (3/8 threads at 100%) ---
https://spark.lucko.me/7duEfJTC9m

--- Profile 2 (7/8 threads at 100%, ~15 min later) ---
https://spark.lucko.me/V1ScooHUAU

Note the specific hot path in both:
GrimPlayer.updateNetherPortalState() 
  -> CompensatedWorld.containsNetherPortal() 
    -> Collisions.hasMaterial() 
      -> CompensatedWorld.getChunk() 
        -> Long2ObjectOpenHashMap.get()


This grew from 42.64% to 62.50% of total Netty IO thread time as the 
incident escalated, and Long2ObjectOpenHashMap.get() specifically from 
22.00% to 32.54%.

Since this executes synchronously inside the Netty decode pipeline (not 
the main server tick thread), TPS remains normal throughout the incident, 
but new/existing player connections suffer severe read timeouts.

How to replicate? Not fully understood on our end. Happy to provide another information, if necessary.

Velocity logs - https://mclo.gs/2llo5Ow

title: Fix NPE by using PlayerManager.getUser over manual channel
body:
## How do I reproduce this?
Use SoulFire to make bots quickly connect to and disconnect from the server.

## Root cause
https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/commit/90036e2bf2eaaf365e091ee884b120fbd8553682 added direct channel → User lookup in `BukkitPlatformPlayer` constructor:
```java
Object channel = PacketEvents.getAPI().getProtocolManager().getChannel(uuid);
this.user = PacketEvents.getAPI().getProtocolManager().getUser(channel);
```
`ProtocolManager.getChannel(UUID)` returns null once the channel has been removed from PacketEvents internal map - which happens on disconnect, protocol switch, or for NPCs without a real channel. The null is passed unconditionally to `getUser()`, which bottoms out in `channel.pipeline()`.

## Verification
Tested using the same method mentioned in **How do I reproduce this?**, error is now gone.

## References
* Fixes https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/issues/2418
* Regression introduced by https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/commit/90036e2bf2eaaf365e091ee884b120fbd8553682

title: Fireworkrocket boost
Fix block predictions getting stranded, leaving permanent ghost blocks
body:
`handlePredictionConfirmation` iterates `serverIsCurrentlyProcessingThesePredictions` and breaks on the first entry with a sequence newer than the confirmed one. The map is an `Int2ObjectOpenHashMap` though, so iteration order has nothing to do with sequence order, and with several predictions in flight a confirmed entry can sit behind a newer one and never get applied.

Once that happens the block is stuck in its client-predicted state: the leftover entry in `originalServerBlocks` also makes `updateBlock` return early for every later server block update at that position, so even resending the chunk doesn't recover it.

Repro: stand on a block and dig it in a place where the break gets cancelled and the block resent (WorldGuard region for example). After enough breaks grim starts simulating the player falling through a block the client is standing on, and the setbacks/simulation flags follow.

The second commit drops prediction state on world change, since the client throws its predictions away together with the old level. A confirmation arriving after the switch could otherwise write an old-world block back into the new world, or move the tracked player position back to the pre-teleport one stored with the prediction.

title: fix five incorrect conditions in the movement simulation
body:
Five independent fixes in the movement simulation, each in its own commit. They are all cases where a condition could never be true, or where the code did not match what the client actually does. None of them change any threshold or add a heuristic.

### What changed

**`fix eye in lava check reading the water level`**
The lava branch of `updateFluidOnEyes` called `getWaterFluidLevelAt`, the same call as the water branch above it. Since that branch already returns when it matches, the lava branch could never be true. Adds a `double` overload of `getLavaFluidLevelAt` so the call reads the same way as the water one.

**`fix strider collision check comparing an entity with itself`**
`hasPassenger` was called on the entity being tested, which can never be true, so the check never filtered anything out. It should skip striders riding the player's own strider, the way the boat check just below it does.

**`fix AxisUtil.combine returning boxes with swapped corners`**
Two of the three branches used `maxY` where `minY` was meant and `minX` where `maxX` was meant, producing boxes with no width and no height. Nothing calls this method at the moment, so this is a correctness fix only.

**`match vanilla when picking between blocks at the same distance`**
When two blocks are the same distance away, vanilla compares them by Y, then Z, then X, and keeps the greater one. The old code compared Y the other way round, fell through instead of deciding when the Y values differed, and added the X and Z differences together, which does not give the same answer as comparing them one after the other. For example `(0, y, 5)` and `(5, y, 0)` sum to the same thing on both axes, while comparing Z separates them.

**`remove leftover eye offset in the 1.21.12+ fluid check`**
`EntityFluidInteraction` kept the `0.1111111119389534` offset from the older `updateFluidOnEyes` code. Vanilla uses the plain eye height here, so the eye was tracked slightly lower than the client has it, which can keep the swimming pose on for a moment too long. The offset is still correct in `PlayerBaseTick`, which is the path older clients take.

### Version and platform reach

Nothing here is platform specific — all of it is in `common`, no new API is used.

Version-wise, each fix only takes effect where the corresponding client code path runs, and none of them change behaviour on versions they do not apply to:

| Fix | Affected clients |
| --- | --- |
| Lava eye level | 1.8 and up (path used up to 1.21.11) |
| Strider collision | 1.8 and up |
| `AxisUtil.combine` | none currently, no callers |
| Supporting block tie-break | 1.20 and up, older clients do not use the supporting block position |
| Fluid eye offset | 1.21.12 and up, older clients go through `PlayerBaseTick` |

The two eye-level fixes are deliberately split so the older and newer paths stay independent: the offset is kept in `PlayerBaseTick` and only dropped in `EntityFluidInteraction`.

### Notes for review

The tie-break change is the one worth a close look, since it is the only one that can change an outcome on a currently reachable path. The order it now implements is the one `Vec3i#compareTo` gives (Y, then Z, then X, greater wins), matching `findSupportingBlock`.

The `AxisUtil` and lava eye-level fixes have no observable effect today — the first has no callers, the second has no reader of `isEyeInFluid(LAVA)` on that path. They are included because leaving a condition that can never be true is a trap for whoever wires them up later.

title: Optimize BlockPlace check dispatch
body:
Builds callback-specific arrays from the registered `BlockPlaceCheck` instances during `CheckManager` initialization.
A cached `ClassValue` identifies callback overrides from each method's declaring class. Each dispatch path iterates only its corresponding filtered array.

title: Optimize rolling punishment violation tracking
body:
Indexes rolling punishment violations with an insertion-ordered primitive map and identity-based primitive counters.
Uses monotonic millisecond timestamps for ordered expiry, removes each expired entry in average constant time, and trims oversized backing arrays after large drains.

title: Skip inapplicable checks during dispatch
body:
Filters `CheckManager` dispatch arrays once during initialization using a per-check `isApplicable()` hook.
Version-specific checks implement the hook with immutable client and server protocol conditions. 

`BadPacketsH` is left ungated because its `CANCELLED_DIGGING` path currently runs outside `isSupportedVersion()`.

title: Fix legacy compatibility and proxy alert exceptions
body:
## Summary

- Guard legacy fluid-flow handling from reading the `LEVEL` property on water-like block states that do not define it.
- Treat bubble columns as source water for legacy liquid-depth calculations.
- Disable proxy alert send/receive checks while Grim's configuration is transiently unavailable during startup or reload.
- Encode entity types unavailable to legacy clients as an explicit unknown sentinel in verbose Reach data.

## Root cause

Legacy fluid prediction assumed every state classified as water exposed `StateValue.LEVEL`. Bubble columns are water-like but do not have that property, so movement processing could throw while reading their level.

Proxy alert packet handling also assumed the active configuration was always non-null. Packets arriving during a startup or reload transition could race with configuration replacement and repeatedly throw.

Reach verbose output wrote PacketEvents' per-client entity ID directly to an unsigned field. Entity types unavailable in an older client version produce `-1`, causing verbose serialization to throw instead of recording the Reach result.

## Impact

These guards prevent all three exception paths without changing normal behavior once valid state is available. Legacy clients can move around bubble columns without triggering the fluid-level failure, proxy alert packets safely no-op during short configuration transitions, and unsupported entity types render as `unknown` without interrupting Reach processing.

## Validation

- `gradlew :common:test :bukkit:build`
- Added regression coverage for supported and unsupported verbose entity IDs.
- Built and deployed the patched Bukkit jar on Leaf 1.21.11.
- Restarted the server and ran `grim reload`; the console remained clean while players reconnected.

title: Ghost block remains client-side after block placement on Fabric
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it
### Description

Sometimes when a player places a block, the block appears normally on the client but does not seem to actually exist on the server.

The block becomes a persistent client-side ghost block.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Fabric 26.1.2 server with Grim enabled.
2. Place blocks normally.
3. Occasionally, a placed block becomes a ghost block.
4. Break the affected block.
5. No item is dropped, suggesting that the block never actually existed server-side.
6. Try to jump or stand on the affected position.
7. The client still appears to have collision with the ghost block and the player can get stuck.
8. Disconnect and reconnect to the server.
9. The ghost block disappears immediately after reconnecting.

### Expected behavior

If a block placement is rejected or cancelled, the client should be resynchronized with the actual server block state immediately.

### Actual behavior

The client continues to render the block and retain its collision until the player reconnects.

The default Grim block resynchronization handler is enabled:

```yaml
disable-default-resync-handler: false
````

I have not yet identified which specific block placement check triggers the issue.

I can provide verbose output or additional testing if needed.

### Grim version

2.3.74-2614909

### Server version

Fabric 26.1.2

### Client version

Fabric 1.21.11-26.1.2

Fabric

title: Bubble columns causes falses while colliding horizontally in 26.2
body: ### Describe the false positive and how to replicate it https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23b61f02-22bd-4866-a9a8-469ff8d3d69c I have searched existing github issues, and found this https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/issues/2559 , which is very likely related in terms of reproduction condition, (stole the title from that issue). I am opening a new issue here instead of re-opening the old one, I would assume for that issue at that version, it is fixed already. Not sure if there is anything changed for 26.2(I don't know anything about what changed between versions), but based on what I see already in the [mc source](https://mcsrc.dev/1/26.2/net/minecraft/world/level/block/BubbleColumnBlock#L57), I suspect it maybe related to this, it has a condition guard for `isPrecise`. Which then is called by applyEffectsFromBlocks, and the condition is calculated [as such](https://mcsrc.dev/1/26.2/net/minecraft/world/entity/Entity#L1368). That's what I found when I was implementing related in my azalea branch, what I found missing, was that azalea used to dedupe based on travel `BlockState`s, and now it is changed to `BlockPos` with this `isPrecise` flag. And in regression testing for the bubble column in the same path(for handling entity in block effects) I found grim flags azalea, and later I was able to verify with a vanilla client. I have specifically created a new instance of both paper and vanilla client without any mods just to reproduce this cleanly. ### Grim Log https://paste.grim.ac/fDRejUvjWB ### Grim version `Grim Version: 2.3.74-2614909` ### Server version `Paper version 26.2-47-main@ad5d26a` ### Client version Vanilla 26.2 (Launched from PrismLauncher, absolutly no mod) ### Plugins/Mods ``` > plugins [17:22:40 INFO]: ℹ Server Plugins (1): [17:22:40 INFO]: Bukkit Plugins: [17:22:40 INFO]: - GrimAC ```

title: Fix/issue 2775
body:
***

Fixes #2775

**What changed:**
- Replaced `player.getClientVersion()` with the server's version when retrieving the entity type ID in the `Reach` check verbose output, as suggested by the maintainers.
- Wrapped the returned entity ID in `Math.max(0, ...)` to ensure that unmapped or custom entities do not return `-1` and cause an `IllegalArgumentException` in `VerboseBuf.uint`.

**Why:**
This resolves the console spam and internal error caused by `-1` values bypassing the unsigned integer encoder during the Reach check.

***

title: Fabric 26.2 crash: NoClassDefFoundError for net.kyori.adventure.util.Buildable$Builder
body:
## Description
GrimAC crashes the Fabric 26.2 server during startup when its update checker attempts to send a message. The failure is a `NoClassDefFoundError` for `net.kyori.adventure.util.Buildable$Builder`.

## Environment
- Minecraft: Fabric 26.2
- GrimAC: `2.3.74-5920e74`
- Fabric API: `0.157.0+26.2`

title: ElytraJump
Fake "swimming" pose from GSit's crawl feature fully bypasses movement/fly checks (no real water contact required)
body:
### Describe the bypass and how to replicate it

Grim trusts the player's self-sent "swimming" pose bit (0x10 in the metadata byte at index 0) as ground truth for `GrimPlayer#isSwimming`, without checking whether the player is actually touching a liquid block. Any plugin that calls the vanilla `Player#setSwimming(true)` API while the player is on dry land/in open air will make Grim switch that player onto its swimming movement model, which allows free omnidirectional movement (including vertical, with no gravity check) - exactly like real vanilla water physics, just applied outside of water. This is not a false-positive fix, it's a full checks bypass: a client can move freely through the air for as long as the fake pose stays active, with nothing flagged.

I found this via the GSit plugin, whose crawl feature spoofs the swimming pose specifically to shrink the player's hitbox (it never actually puts the player in water):

`dev/geco/gsit/mcv/v1_21_11/model/Crawl.java` (identical in every per-version module):
```java
@Override
public void start() {
    player.setSwimming(true);   // real state change, player is NOT in a liquid
    ...
}

@Override
public void stop() {
    ...
    player.setSwimming(false);
}
```

Grim then reads that pose bit unconditionally in `PacketSelfMetadataListener.java` (lines 76-96):
```java
boolean isSwimming = (field & 0x10) == 0x10;
...
player.latencyUtils.addRealTimeTask(player.lastTransactionSent.get(), () -> {
    player.isSwimming = isSwimming;
    ...
});
```
No check against the player's actual block/eye position (water/bubble column) is done before accepting this.

`player.isSwimming` then feeds directly into the swimming movement branches in `PredictionEngine.java` (~lines 259, 732, 742, 747), which grant the same movement freedom real swimming has.

Grim already has a precedent for this exact class of problem on the elytra side - `manager/player/features/types/ExemptElytraFeature.java` + the `exempt-elytra` config option exist because third-party plugins fake the gliding pose bit (0x80) too. There is no equivalent safeguard for the swimming pose bit (0x10); it's implicitly trusted at all times.

**Why this hasn't surfaced from vanilla behavior before:** vanilla itself reuses this exact same swimming pose/flag for the "crawling through a <1.5-block gap" mechanic on dry land, so trusting the bit isn't wrong in principle. But vanilla only ever enters that pose when the player is physically boxed in by a low ceiling - per the vanilla mechanic, this pose can't be entered at all unless standing/sneaking would otherwise cause head collision ("a player cannot crawl when there is no risk of suffocation"). So even with relaxed movement checks, the surrounding block collision itself keeps the player pinned in place - there is nowhere to "fly" to. GSit's crawl removes that implicit constraint: it calls `setSwimming(true)` unconditionally on command, with no requirement that the player be enclosed by anything above them, so the same trusted flag now grants the relaxed movement model in wide-open air with nothing to physically confine it. In other words, the bit itself was never an unsafe signal on its own - it was only ever safe because it was previously impossible to set without also being trapped by real collision, and that implicit assumption is what breaks here.

Steps to replicate:
1. Install GSit alongside Grim (GSit's crawl permission `GSit.Crawl` defaults to `true`, so any regular player has access, no OP needed).
2. As any player, trigger crawl mode with `/crawl`.
3. While crawling, move freely through open air (e.g. step off a ledge, or ascend) using any client-side movement manipulation (modified client / packet injection).
4. No Fly/Speed/NoFall check is triggered - the player can sustain altitude and move freely in any direction for as long as crawl stays active.
5. Run `/crawl` again to stop crawling - normal checks resume immediately.

Suggested fix: before granting the swimming movement model / relaxed checks based on `isSwimming`, verify the condition vanilla itself requires for this pose to be legitimate - either the player is actually touching a liquid/bubble-column block (Grim already has the primitives for this, e.g. the fluid-contact check used for `pointThreeEstimator.isNearFluid`), or the player is genuinely confined by a solid block close overhead (the same head-collision condition vanilla requires to enter the crawl pose on land in the first place). If neither can be confirmed, either ignore the pose-derived `isSwimming` for movement-model selection, or add an admin-configurable `exempt-swimming`-style flag mirroring `exempt-elytra`.

### Grim version

2.3.74-9eaf917

### Server version

Paper 1.21.11

### Client version

1.21.11

### Plugins/Mods

GSit, GrimAC

title: Required resource-pack configuration time is counted toward transaction timeout
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

Grim can disconnect a healthy client with `disconnect.timeout` while the client is still in the CONFIGURATION state downloading/applying a required server resource pack.

#### Reproduction

1. Run modern Paper with `require-resource-pack=true` and a sufficiently large resource pack.
2. Install Grim and leave `max-transaction-time` at 60 seconds (or use 120 seconds and throttle the pack download accordingly).
3. Connect a vanilla client and make the resource-pack download/application take longer than that limit.
4. Keep the Minecraft TCP connection healthy throughout configuration.
5. Grim disconnects the client at `max-transaction-time`, even though no Grim transaction can be sent in this state.

#### Observed production timeline

A 29,372,229-byte required pack produced this packet-level timeline:

- `+1.4s`: vanilla client reports resource pack `ACCEPTED`
- `+78.7s`: client reports `DOWNLOADED`
- `+113.7s`: client reports `SUCCESSFULLY_LOADED`
- `+113.8s`: Paper sends finish-configuration
- `+120.9s`: Grim logs `Disconnecting <player> for disconnect.timeout`

During the entire interval, bidirectional TCP remained healthy and the client returned Paper's configuration keepalive IDs approximately once per second. The finish-configuration TCP segment was also acknowledged. Another active client remained connected, and there was no server, proxy, Docker, NIC, or packet-loss event.

Increasing `max-transaction-time` from 120 to 180 avoids this particular occurrence but is only a workaround.

#### Relevant Grim logic

`playerClockAtLeast` is initialized when `GrimPlayer` is constructed:

https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/blob/f803be6f7dd931f67753bf71954660bf0f2d25a6/common/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/player/GrimPlayer.java#L137

`sendTransaction` correctly refuses to send outside PLAY:

https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/blob/f803be6f7dd931f67753bf71954660bf0f2d25a6/common/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/player/GrimPlayer.java#L488-L491

However, `pollData` enforces the timeout without checking the connection state or whether a transaction has ever been sent:

https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/blob/f803be6f7dd931f67753bf71954660bf0f2d25a6/common/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/player/GrimPlayer.java#L563-L574

Therefore CONFIGURATION time is charged against a transaction deadline that the client cannot satisfy. The current `2.0` head (`f803be6`) still has the same logic.

Expected behavior: transaction timeout accounting should begin/reset when PLAY is entered or when the first PLAY transaction is sent, and it should not disconnect a player while no Grim transaction can be sent.

### Grim version

`2.3.74-1821c3e`

Also confirmed that current `2.0` head `f803be6f7dd931f67753bf71954660bf0f2d25a6` retains the relevant logic.

### Server version

Paper `26.1.2-74-ver/26.1.2@e4e17fc`, Minecraft `26.1.2`, Java 25.

The Paper server is behind Velocity. ViaVersion translates a protocol-776 client to the protocol-775 backend.

### Client version

Vanilla Minecraft `26.2`, protocol `776`.

### Affected Platform(s)

Bukkit

### Plugins/Mods

Paper plugins: AuthMeVelocity, BetterModel, CommandPanels, CrazyCrates, ExcellentEnchants, FancyNpcs, GeyserModelEngine, SkBee, SmartSpawner, nightcore.

Bukkit plugins: AdventureCore, AnnouncementCenter, AntiPopup, AttributeSwapFixer, AuctionBackpackReturns, AuctionExtras, AuctionItemSelector, AuraSkills, AuthMe, AuthMePremiumBukkit, AuthMeUI, AxAFKZone, AxPlayerWarps, AxTrade, BattleArena, BestTools, BetonQuest, BetterMOTD, BetterRTP, CMILib, ChatGames, Chunky, ConsoleSpamFixReborn, CoreProtect, DecentHolograms, DiscordSRV, Essentials, FastAsyncWorldEdit, GeyserUtils, GriefPrevention, GrimAC, InteractionVisualizer, InvSeePlusPlus, LibsDisguises, LuckPerms, Multiverse-Core, MythicMobs, PlaceholderAPI, PlayerAuctions, ProtocolLib, SimpleVoteGems, SkinsRestorer, Skript, TAB, UltimateTimber, Vault, ViaBackwards 5.11.0, ViaVersion 5.11.0, WildernessDungeonPoolHelper, WorldGuard, WorldwideChat, floodgate, PacketEvents 2.13.0, skript-placeholders, skript-reflect, skript-worldguard, skript-yaml, voicechat.

title: # GrimAC crashes on startup when HuskHomes is present (Fabric, MC 26.2) — `NoClassDefFoundError: Buildable$Builder`
body:
### Stack trace

# GrimAC crashes on startup when HuskHomes is present (Fabric, MC 26.2) — `NoClassDefFoundError: Buildable$Builder`

## Summary

GrimAC crashes during server startup with a `NoClassDefFoundError` for `net.kyori.adventure.util.Buildable$Builder`, but only when **HuskHomes** is also installed. Removing HuskHomes lets GrimAC start normally every time; re-adding it reproduces the crash every time. This looks like a shaded Adventure library collision between the two mods rather than a Minecraft-version issue.

## Environment

- **GrimAC:** `2.3.74-155abaf` (Fabric)
- **Minecraft:** `26.2`
- **Fabric Loader:** `0.19.3`
- **Java:** 25 (Eclipse Adoptium)
- **Server type:** Dedicated server (hosted, headless)
- **HuskHomes:** `4.11-7a2d09a` (Fabric)

Other mods present at the time (for context, none of these appear to be involved in the crash):
architectury 21.0.7, cloth-config 26.2.155, economycraft 1.8.0, fabric-api 0.158.0+26.2, flan 26.2-1.12.8-fabric, lithostitched 1.8.0+beta3, luckperms 5.5.57, terralith 2.6.4.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a Fabric 26.2 server with GrimAC `2.3.74-155abaf` installed (no HuskHomes). Start the server.
   - **Result:** GrimAC initializes successfully, no errors.
2. Add HuskHomes `4.11-7a2d09a` to the `mods` folder alongside GrimAC. Restart the server.
   - **Result:** Server crashes during startup (see stack trace below).
3. Remove HuskHomes again, restart.
   - **Result:** GrimAC starts fine again, confirming HuskHomes is the trigger.

This was verified in both directions (remove → works, re-add → crashes again) to rule out coincidence.

## Expected Behavior

GrimAC should start successfully regardless of whether HuskHomes is installed.

## Actual Behavior

Server crashes on startup while GrimAC's update checker tries to send itself a chat message:

```
java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: net/kyori/adventure/util/Buildable$Builder
	at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.defineClass1(Native Method)
	at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.defineClass(ClassLoader.java:962)
	at java.base/java.security.SecureClassLoader.defineClass(SecureClassLoader.java:144)
	at net.fabricmc.loader.impl.launch.knot.KnotClassLoader.defineClassFwd(KnotClassLoader.java:165)
	at net.fabricmc.loader.impl.launch.knot.KnotClassDelegate.tryLoadClass(KnotClassDelegate.java:368)
	at net.fabricmc.loader.impl.launch.knot.KnotClassDelegate.loadClass(KnotClassDelegate.java:231)
	at net.fabricmc.loader.impl.launch.knot.KnotClassLoader.loadClass(KnotClassLoader.java:119)
	at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:490)
	at knot//ac.grim.grimac.platform.fabric.mc261.Fabric261ConversionUtil.toNativeText(Fabric261ConversionUtil.java:50)
	at knot//ac.grim.grimac.platform.fabric.sender.FabricOfficialSenderFactory.sendMessage(FabricOfficialSenderFactory.java:57)
	at knot//net.minecraft.commands.CommandSourceStack.sendMessage(CommandSourceStack.java:1545)
	at knot//ac.grim.grimac.command.commands.GrimVersion.checkForUpdatesAsync(GrimVersion.java:41)
	at knot//ac.grim.grimac.manager.init.start.UpdateChecker.start(UpdateChecker.java:10)
	at knot//ac.grim.grimac.manager.InitManager.start(InitManager.java:85)
	at knot//ac.grim.grimac.GrimAPI.start(GrimAPI.java:103)
	at knot//ac.grim.grimac.platform.fabric.AbstractGrimACFabricEntryPoint.lambda$initialize$1(AbstractGrimACFabricEntryPoint.java:60)
	at knot//ac.grim.grimac.platform.fabric.FabricServerEvents.fireServerStarting(FabricServerEvents.java:30)
	at knot//net.fabricmc.fabric.api.event.lifecycle.v1.ServerLifecycleEvents.lambda$static$1(ServerLifecycleEvents.java:38)
	at knot//net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.handler$zjf000$fabric-lifecycle-events-v1$beforeSetupServer(MinecraftServer.java:4419)
	at knot//net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.runServer(MinecraftServer.java:741)
	at knot//net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.lambda$spin$0(MinecraftServer.java:320)
	at java.base/java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:1474)
Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: net.kyori.adventure.util.Buildable$Builder
	at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:580)
	at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:490)
	at net.fabricmc.loader.impl.launch.knot.KnotClassDelegate.loadClass(KnotClassDelegate.java:239)
	at net.fabricmc.loader.impl.launch.knot.KnotClassLoader.loadClass(KnotClassLoader.java:119)
	at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:490)
	... 22 more
```

## Suspected Cause

HuskHomes bundles `adventure-platform-fabric 7.1.0`, which pulls in `net.kyori:adventure-api:5.2.0` as its own Fabric sub-mod. GrimAC's Fabric build does not declare a full `adventure-api` dependency of its own (only `adventure-nbt 4.26.1`, bundled transitively via PacketEvents), so it appears to rely on an Adventure copy shaded/compiled directly into its own jar — which is presumably why it works fine when HuskHomes is absent.

When HuskHomes is present, its externally-declared `adventure-api 5.2.0` mod seems to take precedence on the classpath over whatever GrimAC ships internally. The class `net.kyori.adventure.util.Buildable$Builder`, which `Fabric261ConversionUtil.toNativeText` depends on, does not exist in Adventure 5.2.0 (it was part of an older/deprecated Adventure API surface). Neither mod appears to relocate its shaded Adventure package into a private namespace, so the two collide instead of coexisting.

## Suggested Fix

Relocating GrimAC's shaded Adventure dependency into a private package namespace (or updating the Fabric `Fabric261ConversionUtil` code path to work against current Adventure 5.x APIs) would likely resolve the collision.

## Additional Notes

Happy to test a patched/dev build or provide the full mod list / logs if useful.


### How to replicate it if known

just place HusckHomes and AC together, server will crash

### Grim version

**GrimAC:** `2.3.74-155abaf`

### Server version

1.26.2

### Affected Platform(s)

Fabric

HuskHomes

title: Elytra resync leaves players permanently crouched server-side
body:
**Project:** GrimAnticheat/Grim (`2.0`)
**File:** `common/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/events/packets/PacketEntityAction.java`
**Case:** `START_FLYING_WITH_ELYTRA`

## Symptom

Reported by players as: *"while running with an elytra, at some point you are
sneaking and don't know it."* The sneak key is not held and the client shows no
crouch, but the player moves at sneak speed and has a lowered hitbox until
something else resyncs the pose.

## Cause

Both rejection branches resync the pose by inverting the server-side sneak flag
and never restoring it:

```java
// Client ignores sneaking, use it to resync
player.platformPlayer.setSneaking(!player.platformPlayer.isSneaking());
```

That is a toggle, not a pulse. It is correct exactly once. Called an even number
of times the state happens to return to where it started, and called an odd
number of times it latches — and both branches fire repeatedly in ordinary play:

* `player.onGround || player.lastOnGround` fires on every elytra-open attempt
  made while running, and players spam the key when a takeoff does not catch.
* The `!player.canGlide()` branch fires on latency-compensated inventory
  disagreement, which is transient by nature.

Neither branch is rate-limited, so the parity is effectively random. Worse, the
flag also feeds `isSneaking` back into the prediction engine's own view of the
player, so a latched value can go on to affect predictions rather than merely
looking wrong.

## Fix applied downstream

Make it a pulse rather than a toggle: flip the flag, then restore the previous
value on the following tick via the entity scheduler. The resync still reaches
the client — one metadata change in each direction — but the state is
self-cancelling, so no call sequence can leave it latched.

The same pattern appears at a third call site in our fork (`GrimPlayer`, the
generic force-resync path); all three were changed together.

Happy to open a PR if useful.

title: Entities spawned into a new world are wiped by the respawn handler and never return
body:
### Describe the bug

On a world change, entities that have already been spawned into the new world can be wiped from `entityMap` and never come back, leaving them invisible to every check that looks them up for the rest of the player's stay in that world.

This is the same defect as #2772, on the entity side rather than the chunk side. Filing it separately because the symptom is completely different: the chunk case announces itself with an infinite setback loop, this one is silent.

### Mechanism

Entity spawns are applied through a latency task scheduled at the transaction current when the spawn packet was read:

https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/blob/2.0/common/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/events/packets/PacketEntityReplication.java#L540-L544

The respawn handler clears `entityMap` from a task scheduled one transaction later, together with `activePistons` and `openShulkerBoxes`:

https://github.com/GrimAnticheat/Grim/blob/2.0/common/src/main/java/ac/grim/grimac/events/packets/PacketPlayerRespawn.java#L201-L204

Nothing orders those two tasks. If the server spawns entities into the new world before the respawn's trailing transaction is written, their tasks land on the earlier transaction and run first, and the clear removes them. The server does not re-send a spawn packet, because as far as it is concerned the client already has the entity.

### Consequence

A player whose reach, hitbox or interaction checks are evaluated against a wiped entity has that entity simply missing from the anticheat's view. No violation, no loop, no log line — the checks quietly stop covering it. Pistons and shulkers are affected the same way, though far less severely: pistons expire on their own and a shulker only affects one collision box.

### Suggested fix

The same one that works for chunks: stamp each entity with a world generation incremented synchronously while handling the respawn packet, drop inserts belonging to a superseded world, and have the respawn remove only what belongs to worlds the player has left, rather than clearing the map. That makes the result independent of which task happens to run first, instead of trying to order them.

### Grim version

2.0 branch as of 2026-08-28 (mechanism read from source; the chunk-side twin is reproduced and reported in #2772)

title: Reach and Hitboxes never call reward(), so their violations only ever climb
body:
### Question rather than a bug report

`Reach` and `Hitboxes` never call `reward()` — zero occurrences in either file on `2.0`. `Check.reward()` exists and decays violations, and other checks do use it (`AimModulo360`, `BadPacketsR`, `TriggerA`, etc.), so the convention is clearly "reward on a clean result".

Is that deliberate for these two, or an oversight?

The reason I ask: on a fork carrying the GroundedGrim `WallHit`/`EntityPierce` port, which flags from the same `Reach` path and inherits the same absence, violation totals climbed without bound. Production alerts reached VL 2200 on `WallHit` and VL 22600 on `EntityPierce` for ordinary players hitting mobs at a farm. Those numbers are lifetime sums of false positives, not a measure of anything recent, and any punishment threshold built on them ends up firing on how long a player has been online rather than on what they did.

The two ported checks are not yours, and their false positives were our problem to fix (a penetration-depth test rather than a boolean intersection, which sorted them out). But the missing decay is upstream behaviour and applies to `Reach` and `Hitboxes` as well — a long-lived player accumulating occasional borderline hits has no way to work them off.

If it is intentional, it would be worth a comment saying so, because it reads as an omission next to the checks that do reward. If it is not, calling `reward()` when the reach result comes back clean is a one-line change per check.

### Grim version

2.0 branch as of 2026-08-28

title: Fix Fabric 26.2 Adventure 5 incompatibility

This causes Grim's startup update-check message to crash with `NoClassDefFoundError`. This change makes the MC 26.2 module depend on Adventure 5.2.0 and use the native Adventure 5 Gson serializer directly. Related: #2851, #2835, #2800 --- Need help on this PR? title: AntiKB re-sends its own setback velocity, so one setback turns into four or five
body:
When a setback fires, `SetbackTeleportUtil` sends the player a velocity packet. It goes out
through `player.user.sendPacket(...)` rather than `sendPacketSilently`, so it comes straight back
through `KnockbackHandler.onPacketSend` and is recorded as a knockback. `isSendingSetback` is
still true at that point - it's only cleared in the `finally` a few lines below - so the recorded
`VelocityData` gets `isSetback = true`.

On the next tick `onPredictionComplete` reaches this branch:

```java
if (player.likelyKB.isSetback) {
    if (!isNoSetbackPermission()) {
        player.getSetbackTeleportUtil().executeViolationSetback();
    }
}
```

The only thing guarding it is `offset > offsetToFlag`, which defaults to 0.001, so practically any
residual re-sends the setback. That sends another velocity, which comes back as another
`isSetback` knockback, and round it goes.

What makes it self-sustaining is that the teleport in that same method uses `sendPacketSilently`
and only the velocity uses `sendPacket`. If that asymmetry is deliberate I'd be curious what it's
for, because it's the part that closes the loop.

A chain from a 1.16.5 server (our fork, but this code is unmodified from upstream). The vectors
decay exactly like vanilla gravity, because what's being fed back is the setback's own simulated
fall:

```
OffsetHandler setback   vel y=0.3136 -> offset=0.35703 -> resend
resend                  vel y=0.2289 -> offset=0.03684 -> resend
resend                  vel y=0.1459 -> offset=0.06456 -> resend
resend                  vel y=0.0646 -> offset=0.02000 -> resend
```

Four to five setbacks per trigger. Across that whole log, every setback that came out of this
branch had `isSetback = true` - not one of them was a detection, they were all echoes of setbacks
the plugin had just sent itself.

We've patched it locally by requiring the same `immediate` threshold (0.1) the normal path uses,
so a player who really does ignore a resent velocity still gets one but the 0.002-0.06 residuals
don't trigger anything. The chains stopped for us, though it's only been running a couple of
hours, so take that as "looks right" rather than tested. Making the velocity packet silent would
presumably also work and is a smaller change, but I don't know why it isn't silent already.

title: Proxy alert messages can be spoofed by clients connecting directly to the backend when using BungeeCord
body:
### Describe the bug and how to replicate it

When alerts.proxy.receive is enabled, ProxyAlertMessenger accepts GRIMAC messages from the BungeeCord plugin message channel and renders the received alert using MessageUtil.miniMessage(alert).

If the backend server is directly reachable, a client can send a message on the same channel without going through the proxy. Grim currently has no way to distinguish this from a legitimate forwarded alert.

This allows a directly connected client to display arbitrary proxy alerts to staff, including MiniMessage hover and click events. The attached video demonstrates the issue.

Malformed messages can also currently throw out of the PacketEvents listener because part of the payload is parsed before the existing exception handler. I have a small fix for that part and plan to open a separate PR.

The spoofing issue likely needs a different solution since the receiver currently has no way to verify that the message actually originated from the proxy.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfd96291-ed21-417e-b1bf-c7b7895357f2

### Grim version

2.0 (597f559)

### Server version

Paper 26.2

### Client version

26.2

### Affected Platform(s)

Bukkit

### Plugins/Mods

Grim

title: guard proxy alert parsing against malformed client payloads
body: Related to #2868. `ProxyAlertMessenger` currently reads part of the plugin message before entering the existing try/catch. Since clients can send messages on the `BungeeCord` channel themselves, a malformed or truncated payload can throw out of the packet listener. This moves the parsing into the guarded section and rejects invalid message lengths, so malformed payloads are ignored instead of bubbling an exception. This does not fix the spoofing described in #2868. A client connected directly to the backend can still send a correctly formatted forged proxy alert. Preventing that would require a way to verify that the message actually came from the proxy. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.
